title: Automorphic congruences and reverse main-conjecture divisibilities
summary: Target-level plan of AutomorphicCongruences part L0 (stages L0, L1, L2, L2s, L3, L4, L5, L5a; L5b and L5w are the accepted part AutomorphicCongruences--L5b). L0 plans the Σ-primitive Selmer instances, the primitive/imprimitive and specialization comparisons, the Eisenstein ideal, Skinner–Urban's polarized lattice datum and lattice construction with its local conditions, the canonical-period congruence comparison and the Hida–Tilouine anticyclotomic input. L1 plans Skinner–Urban's GU(2,2) argument (ordinary Hermitian forms and Hida theory, the Eisenstein datum, Klingen Eisenstein series by pullback, the three-variable p-adic L-function, the Eisenstein family, coefficient coprimality, the pseudo-character, the Selmer lower bound and Theorems 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.3). L2s plans Castella–Liu–Wan's semi-ordinary GU(3,1) theory and divisibility (Thm 8.2.1 (1) and (2)); L2 plans Fouquet–Wan's general-weight GU(3,1) divisibility (Thm 7.32), Wan's ordinary Rankin–Selberg divisibility, the Kings–Loeffler–Zerbes Beilinson–Flach classes and reciprocity, the Castella–Wan equivalence, the crystalline theorem 4.51 and the §4.8 ordinary reverse divisibility (Thm 1.6). L3 plans Fouquet–Wan's deformation-ring facts, fundamental lines and Nakamura's universal zeta morphism with its specialization to Kato's; L4 plans the descent to the universal-family and pointwise theorems (Thms 5.2, 5.1) and Nakamura's §5 consequences; L5 is an aggregate; L5a plans Burungale–Castella–Skinner's early product divisibility (Prop. 5.2.1) with the ordinary two-variable equivalence (Thm 4.1.3) as an interface to the planned KatoEulerSystems L5 owner. All eight stages are planned; twelve gaps and seventeen requests are recorded; the RS-11 ownership (with its review pending) and the thirteen confirmed red-team findings are followed.

nodes.title: Σ-primitive ordinary Selmer groups over Iwasawa towers
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, A a profinite ℤ_p-algebra, T a free A-module of finite rank with a continuous A-linear G_F-action, and for each place v | p a G_{F_v}-stable A-direct summand T_v ⊆ T with T/T_v free. For a finite set Σ of finite places, Sel^Σ_F(T,(T_v)) is the kernel of the restriction from H¹(F, T ⊗_A A^∨) (A^∨ the Pontryagin dual) to the product over v ∉ Σ, v ∤ p of H¹(I_v, T ⊗ A^∨) and over v | p of H¹(I_v, (T/T_v) ⊗ A^∨): no condition at Σ, unramified elsewhere away from p, and the ordinary (Greenberg) condition at p. Its dual X^Σ_F = Hom_A(Sel^Σ_F, A^∨) is finitely generated over A. For an extension E/F inside a ℤ_p^d-tower, Sel^Σ_E is the direct limit over finite subextensions and X^Σ_E the inverse limit, and Shapiro's lemma identifies Sel^Σ_{F_∞}(T) with Sel^Σ_F(T ⊗_A Λ_{F,A}(ε_F^{-1})) as Λ_{F,A}-modules, where Λ_{F,A} = A ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[Gal(F_∞/F)]] and ε_F is the tautological character. When A is noetherian and normal, Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) denotes the characteristic ideal of X^Σ_F(T) and Ft^Σ_{F,A}(T) its Fitting ideal.
hypotheses: T free of finite rank over the profinite ℤ_p-algebra A, with a continuous action of G_F; T_v free direct summands with free quotients for v | p.
Σ finite; when Σ contains every place where T ramifies and every place above p, the definition reduces to a kernel on H¹(G_{F,Σ}, −).
The characteristic ideal is used only over noetherian normal A, as the divisorial ideal of height-one lengths.
proofSteps: Instantiate the upstream Selmer-structure carrier with the relaxed condition at Σ, the unramified condition at v ∉ Σ ∪ {p} and the Greenberg condition attached to T_v at v | p.
Finite generation of the dual: H¹(G_{F,S}, M ⊗ A^∨) is cofinitely generated for finitely generated M (SU Lemma 3.1.9, after Greenberg).
Shapiro: the coinduced module of A^∨ along Gal(F_n/F) has direct limit Λ_{F,A}^∨(ε_F^{-1}); the restriction maps at v correspond to the products over places of F_n above v (SU 3.1.2, Prop. 3.2.3).
Define Ch^Σ via the height-one length divisor of X^Σ and Ft^Σ via Fitting ideals of a presentation.
acceptance: For T = A(χ) with T_v = 0 at every v | p and Σ ⊇ {places above p} ∪ ram(χ), Sel^Σ_F is the full H¹(G_{F,Σ}, A(χ) ⊗ A^∨).
Enlarging Σ can only enlarge Sel^Σ; the quotient is controlled by local unramified cohomology (L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison).

nodes.title: Primitive against Σ-primitive Selmer groups and the removed Euler factors
nodes.statement: Let T, (T_v) and A be as in L0/sigma-primitive-selmer with A noetherian normal, F = ℚ or an imaginary quadratic field K, and S a finite set of finite places not above p at which T is unramified, contained in Σ. Then (i) Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) ⊇ Ch^{Σ∖S}_{F,A}(T) · ∏_{v∈S} det_A(1 − q_v^{-1} frob_v^{-1} | T) (SU Lemma 3.2.15, Cor. 3.2.16); (ii) over ℚ_∞, the Pontryagin dual of H¹_Σ(ℚ_∞, T ⊗ A^∨) = ∏_{v∈Σ, v∤p} H¹(ℚ_{∞,v}, T ⊗ A^∨) is a finitely generated torsion Λ_{ℚ,A}-module with no nonzero pseudo-null submodule, and its characteristic ideal is generated by ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1} ε_ℚ(frob_ℓ)), P_{T,ℓ}(X) = det(1 − frob_ℓ X | T^{I_ℓ}) (SU Lemma 3.2.17); (iii) when the primitive dual is torsion and the global-to-local map is surjective (Greenberg–Vatsal), Ch^Σ = Ch^∅ · ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}ε(frob_ℓ)) (SU Prop. 3.2.18). On the analytic side the Σ-imprimitive p-adic L-functions are defined by multiplying the primitive ones by the same Euler-factor elements, so every removed factor is matched by the identical element of Λ.
hypotheses: (i) needs only T unramified at S and A noetherian normal; (ii) is over the cyclotomic tower (local Tate duality at each finite level, passed to the limit); (iii) needs torsion of the Σ-primitive dual and surjectivity of the localization map, which SU Prop. 3.2.18 derives from the hypotheses of §3.2.
The Euler factor uses the geometric Frobenius on inertia invariants; at a Steinberg place T^{I_ℓ} has rank one.
proofSteps: (i): the cokernel of Sel^{Σ∖S} → Sel^Σ injects into ∏_{v∈S} H¹(I_v, T ⊗ A^∨)^{G_{F_v}}, whose dual has characteristic ideal det(1 − q_v^{-1}frob_v^{-1}|T) because T is unramified at v.
(ii): Shapiro over ℚ_∞ and local Tate duality compute the local terms; each is Λ-torsion with characteristic ideal the displayed Euler factor, and has no pseudo-null submodule.
(iii): with the localization map surjective the sequence 0 → Sel^∅ → Sel^Σ → H¹_Σ → 0 is exact, and multiplicativity of characteristic ideals gives equality.

Analytic matching: the Σ-imprimitive p-adic L-function is by definition the primitive one times ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_ℓ(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ), so the comparison of characteristic ideals and of analytic functions involves the same elements.
acceptance: The comparison is used in both directions: one-sided bounds are proved for Σ-primitive objects and transferred to the primitive ones without losing a factor.
Steinberg check: for ℓ ∥ N with π_ℓ an unramified twist of Steinberg, the factor is 1 − a_ℓ ℓ^{-1} ε(frob_ℓ) with a_ℓ = ±1, a unit times a distinguished polynomial of degree zero in Λ.

nodes.title: Specializing Σ-primitive Selmer groups and their characteristic ideals
nodes.statement: Let F_∞ be ℚ_∞, K_∞ or K^+_∞, A a profinite ℤ_p-algebra, 𝔞 ⊂ A an ideal and T as in L0/sigma-primitive-selmer. Assume the hypotheses of SU Prop. 3.2.8 (the inertia at p acts on T/T_p through a quotient compatible with the tower, and the relevant H⁰ terms vanish), so that X^Σ_{F_∞}(T)/𝔞 ≅ X^Σ_{F_∞}(T/𝔞T). Then (i) Ft^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T) = Ft^Σ_{F,A}(T) mod 𝔞; (ii) if A and A/𝔞 are noetherian normal domains and (f) ⊇ Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) is principal, then f mod 𝔞 divides Ch^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T); in particular when A is factorial Ch^Σ_{F,A}(T) mod 𝔞 divides Ch^Σ_{F,A/𝔞}(T/𝔞T). (iii) For the descent K_∞ → K^+_∞ along I^- = ker(Λ_K → Λ_ℚ), X^Σ_{K_∞}(T)/I^- ≅ X^Σ_{K^+_∞}(T), and when A is factorial Ch^Σ_{K_∞}(T) mod I^- divides Ch^Σ_{K^+_∞}(T).
hypotheses: The control isomorphism for a general ideal 𝔞 of the coefficient ring is SU Prop. 3.2.8 and is owned here; the upstream derived control (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3) covers the specialization to finite layers of a one-variable tower and is used only there. The control isomorphism needs SU Prop. 3.2.8's hypotheses; without them only a map with kernel and cokernel controlled by H⁰ and local terms exists.
Characteristic ideals do not commute with base change in general; only the principal majorant transfers (ii). A specialization at which f vanishes gives no information.
proofSteps: Fitting ideals commute with base change of a presentation (i).
The characteristic ideal is the smallest divisorial ideal containing the Fitting ideal; a principal ideal is divisorial, so (f) ⊇ Ch ⊇ Ft and reduction gives f mod 𝔞 ∣ Ft(T/𝔞) ⊆ Ch(T/𝔞) (ii).
For (iii), Shapiro along Γ^-_K and Prop. 3.2.8 identify Sel^Σ_{K^+_∞} with the I^- torsion of Sel^Σ_{K_∞}, and (ii) applies.
acceptance: Vanishing check: if f ∈ 𝔞 the conclusion of (ii) is empty, and no cancellation of f against the specialized characteristic ideal is allowed.
Used by L1/su-cyclotomic-divisibility (descent from two variables to the cyclotomic line) and by L5a/quartic-cm-selmer-restriction.

nodes.title: The Eisenstein ideal of an Eisenstein family
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a noetherian complete local domain, 𝕋 a reduced finite Λ-algebra generated over Λ by the images of a set 𝒯 of Hecke operators acting on a space of Λ-adic cusp forms, and λ: 𝒯 → Λ the system of eigenvalues of a Λ-adic Eisenstein family E (a Λ-algebra homomorphism from the abstract Hecke algebra). The Eisenstein ideal I_E ⊆ 𝕋 is the ideal generated by t − λ(t) for t ∈ 𝒯; when the structure map Λ → 𝕋/I_E is surjective, the Eisenstein ideal of Λ is its kernel E_E, so that Λ/E_E ≅ 𝕋/I_E. When I_E is proper, 𝕋_E denotes the localization of 𝕋 at the maximal ideal containing I_E.
hypotheses: 𝕋 is generated over Λ by 𝒯 together with the U_p-operators, so Λ → 𝕋/I_E is surjective; otherwise E_E is defined as the kernel on the image.
The Hecke operators are those at primes outside a fixed finite set Σ, the U_p-operators, and the central or diamond operators used by the source.
proofSteps: Define I_E as the ideal generated by {t − λ(t) : t ∈ 𝒯} and E_E := ker(Λ → 𝕋/I_E).
Surjectivity follows because the generators of 𝕋 over Λ act by scalars of Λ modulo I_E.
acceptance: The congruence statements of L1, L2 and L2s are lower bounds ord_P(E_E) ≥ ord_P(L) for height-one primes P of Λ, from a cuspidal family congruent to E.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban lattice datum
nodes.statement: Let H = G ⋊ {1, c} with c of order two, A a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field F and maximal ideal m, and R a local reduced finite flat A-algebra with R/M = A/m. A lattice datum consists of: (1) a character ν: H → A^×; (2) a character χ: G → A^× with χ̄ ≠ ν̄χ̄^{-c}, and χ′ := νχ^{-c}; (3) a representation ρ: G → Aut_A(V), V ≅ A^n, with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ ν, ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and ρ residually disjoint from χ and χ′ (some x ∈ A[G] has coprime residual characteristic polynomials); (4) a representation σ: G → Aut_{R⊗F}(M), M ≅ (R ⊗ F)^{n+2}, with σ^c ≅ σ^∨ ⊗ ν, tr σ(G) ⊆ R and finitely generated R[G]-orbits; (5) a proper ideal I ⊂ R with J := A ∩ I ≠ 0, A/J ≅ R/I and tr σ ≡ χ′ + tr ρ + χ mod I. Local data at a subgroup D ⊂ G: a D-stable free summand M^+ ⊆ M with free quotient, a D-stable free summand V^+ ⊆ V, and the congruence Ch(M^+, x, T) ≡ Ch(V^+, x, T)(1 − Tχ(x)) mod I for x ∈ R[D]. The datum is ν-polarized when ν is compatible (Φ^t = −ν(c)Φ) with the polarization of ρ.
hypotheses: The polarization conditions are those of SU 4.2.2; residual disjointness is in the sense of SU 4.1.2.

In applications G = G_{K,Σ}, H = G_{ℚ,Σ}, D a decomposition group at a prime above p, A the completion of a localization of a two-variable Iwasawa algebra at a height-one prime P, and R a completed local Hecke algebra.
proofSteps: Record the data (1)–(5) and the local data 4.5.1–4.5.3 as fields; derive the congruence for the quotients M^- and V^- from 4.3.1.
Residual disjointness gives projectors x_1, x_2 ∈ B[G] with x_i acting as identity on one summand and zero on the other (SU Lemma 4.1.3, via the Henselian property).
acceptance: The SU instance (SU 7.3.2), the CLW instance (proof of CLW Thm 8.2.1, items (1)–(5)) and the FW instance (proof of FW Thm 7.32) are all lattice data with n = 2.

nodes.title: The lattice construction: Eisenstein ideals bound Selmer groups
nodes.statement: Let (ν, χ, ρ, σ, I) be a ν-polarized lattice datum (L0/su-lattice-datum) with H = G_{ℚ,Σ}, G = G_{K,Σ}, local data at D = G_{K,p} satisfying SU 4.5.1–4.5.3, with V^+_0 ⊕ A(χ) and V^-_0 ⊕ A(χ′) residually disjoint modulo P, where A = Â_{0,P} for a height-one prime P of a noetherian normal domain A_0, and J = A ∩ I. Then (i) ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) ≥ ℓ_P(L(χ′)/J(χ′)); (ii) ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ℓ_P(N/N′), and in particular ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ord_P(J) when N′ = 0 (SU Prop. 4.5.6); (iii) if ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) = 0 then ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ ord_P(J) (SU Cor. 4.5.7); (iv) under SU Lemma 4.3.11, if ord_P(J) > ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) then ord_P Ch^Σ_K(ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1}) ≥ 1 (SU Prop. 4.5.8). Here the Selmer groups are the Σ-primitive ones of L0/sigma-primitive-selmer for the pairs (A_0(ψν), 0) and (V_0(χ^{-1}), V^+_0(χ^{-1})). The variant of Wan20 Prop. 9.2 replaces the irreducibility of σ by condition (9): every specialization σ_λ is absolutely irreducible or contains an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional subrepresentation with trace ≡ χ + χ^{-c} modulo I.
hypotheses: P is a height-one prime of A_0 with A_0 noetherian normal; the polarization ν is compatible with the polarization of ρ (4.5.5.a).
The bound concerns the Σ-primitive groups; primitive versions follow by L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison.
The excluded case ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) > 0 is where the abelian Selmer group may absorb the extensions; CLW and Wan exclude such P explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose a lattice ℒ ⊂ M stable under R[G]; the residual projectors of the datum decompose ℒ into pieces ℒ(χ′), ℒ(ρ), ℒ(χ) with submodules 𝒥(·) cut out by I (SU 4.3, Cor. 4.3.9).

Off-diagonal blocks define cocycles: φ ↦ c_φ(g) = (φ ⊗ id)(χ^{-1}(g)σ(g)ε̄* − ε̄*) gives Hom_{A_0}(N, A_0^∨) → H¹(G, V_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})), whose dual is surjective after localizing at P (SU Props 4.4.4–4.4.5).

Local conditions: the projector x^+ ∈ R[D] splits the D-extension, so a multiple t ∉ P of the image lies in the kernel of restriction to H¹(D, V^-_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})), i.e. satisfies the ordinary condition (SU Prop. 4.5.4); by polarization the same holds at the conjugate prime.
Lengths: the dual Selmer group surjects onto Hom(N, A_0^∨)^∨ localized at P, giving (ii); (iii) and (iv) follow from (i), Lemma 4.3.8 and Lemma 4.3.11.
For the Wan20 variant, condition (9) replaces the use of irreducibility in the construction of ℒ; the rest is unchanged.
acceptance: A height-one prime with ord_P(J) = 2 and N′ = 0 must give ord_P(Ch) ≥ 2, not just ≥ 1.
Excluded-prime check: when ord_P Ch^Σ_ℚ(ψν) > 0 and Lemma 4.3.11 fails, no conclusion is drawn.
The extension classes are those of the automorphic family; the theorem does not presuppose any divisibility of characteristic ideals.

nodes.title: Local conditions satisfied by the automorphic extension classes
nodes.statement: In the situation of L0/lattice-construction, the classes [c_φ] obtained from the off-diagonal blocks of σ satisfy, after multiplication by an element t ∉ P: (a) at every place v ∉ Σ they are unramified, since σ is unramified outside Σ; (b) at the primes above p they lie in the kernel of restriction to H¹(D, V^-_0 ⊗ A_0^∨(χ^{-1})) for D = G_{K,p} (the ordinary condition), and by the polarization the corresponding statement holds at G_{K,p̄}; (c) at places v ∈ Σ, v ∤ p, no condition is imposed (Σ-primitive). When v = ℓ ∈ Σ is a place where π_ℓ is an unramified twist of Steinberg, the transfer from the Σ-primitive to the primitive Selmer group uses the rank-one inertia invariants T^{I_ℓ} and the Euler factor det(1 − ℓ^{-1}frob_ℓ | T^{I_ℓ}) of L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison; the residual hypothesis that ρ̄ be ramified at ℓ (SU 3.6.1, FW Thm 1.6(2)) makes this factor a unit at the relevant height-one primes.
hypotheses: The residual disjointness of V^+ ⊕ A(χ) and V^- ⊕ A(χ′) modulo P (SU (7.3.3.a)) is what produces the D-projector; it is verified in each instance (SU proof of Thm 7.3.5, CLW and FW checks).
proofSteps: (a) σ, hence every block, factors through G_{K,Σ}.
(b) is SU Prop. 4.5.4(ii): the projector x^+ acts as identity on M^+ and kills M^-, so the extension restricted to D splits along the filtration.

Steinberg places: local Tate duality and the rank-one inertia invariants give the Euler factor; ramification of ρ̄ at ℓ makes T^{I_ℓ} ⊗ k one-dimensional with Frobenius eigenvalue ±1 not congruent to ℓ (FW Assumption 3.7).
acceptance: Checks the three kinds of local condition named by the stage: unramified, Steinberg via relaxing and Euler factors, ordinary at p.

nodes.title: Canonical periods, Petersson norms and the congruence number
nodes.statement: Let f be an ordinary eigenform in a Hida family 𝐟 with coefficients in a normal domain 𝕀 satisfying (irred) and (dist). The congruence module of the cuspidal Hecke algebra at the augmentation λ_f is cyclic and generated by the congruence number η_f (PadicFamilies:L1/congruence-module, congruence-ideal); with the canonical periods Ω^±_f defined by the integral modular-symbol lattice, ⟨f, f^c|(−1/N)⟩/(Ω^+_f Ω^-_f) generates η_f up to a p-adic unit. Consequently the SU three-variable p-adic L-function normalized by Ω^+Ω^- (Thm 12.3.1(ii)) is integral, while the version normalized by the Petersson norm (Thm 12.3.1(i)) has denominators bounded by η_f; and every Fourier coefficient of the Eisenstein family divided by Ω^+Ω^- (Thms 12.4.1–12.4.2) is integral. No comparison between the canonical periods Ω^±_f and the Gross period (a quaternionic or toric normalization) is asserted: Fouquet–Wan note that such a comparison is not available in the needed generality, and this packet records it as a gap rather than a lemma.
hypotheses: (irred) and (dist) for f, which give the freeness of the relevant Hecke modules and the Gorenstein property used to make the congruence module cyclic.
The unit u_{f_φ} in SU Thm 12.3.1(ii) depends only on f_φ and is not specified further.
proofSteps: Hida's congruence formula: the congruence module of the Hecke algebra at f is O/η_f with η_f = ⟨f,f⟩/(Ω^+Ω^-) up to unit, via the integral Eichler–Shimura pairing on modular symbols (PadicFamilies:L1/family-period-line, period-change-of-trivialisation).
SU Lemma 12.2.7 produces both the Petersson-normalized element 𝐼_g and the integral element 𝑁_g; their ratio is the family congruence number.
Record the canonical/Gross period question as the gap 'canonical-gross-periods'.
acceptance: The integral normalization is the one in which the lattice construction measures congruences; replacing Ω^+Ω^- by a non-integral period breaks the integrality of E_D's coefficients.

nodes.title: The Hida–Tilouine anticyclotomic main conjecture for CM fields (one divisibility and equality)
nodes.statement: Let M be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F, p an odd prime unramified in M with every prime of F above p split in M, Σ an ordinary CM type, and ψ a branch character. For the anticyclotomic Katz–Hida–Tilouine p-adic L-function L^-_ψ and the Iwasawa module X^-_ψ of the anticyclotomic tower (the ψ-part of the Galois group of the maximal p-abelian extension unramified outside Σ_p), under the hypotheses of Hida–Tilouine (ψ residually nontrivial on the relevant decomposition groups) and Hida 2006, the characteristic ideal of X^-_ψ equals the ideal generated by L^-_ψ (after Hida's μ = 0 theorem, integrally). The congruence-module method proves char(X^-_ψ) ⊆ (L^-_ψ) by comparing the congruence module of a CM Hida family with the anticyclotomic L-value, and Rubin's or the class-number argument gives the other direction.
hypotheses: Hypotheses as in Hida–Tilouine (Invent. Math. 117, 1994, and Ann. Sci. ÉNS 26, 1993) and Hida (Doc. Math. extra volume Coates, 2006); they were not read for this packet, so the exact list is a recorded gap.
proofSteps: Construct the CM Hida family attached to ψ and its congruence module; identify the congruence ideal with the anticyclotomic L-value (Hida–Tilouine).
Use the lattice construction for CM families to bound X^-_ψ below by the congruence module.

Combine with the analytic class number formula along the tower, or Rubin's main conjecture when F = ℚ, for the reverse inequality; Hida's μ = 0 (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/hida-katz-mu-vanishing) removes the p-ambiguity.
acceptance: Consumed by L2s/clw-integrality (CLW's integrality of L_{π,K,ξ} through L^Hida) and requested by HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8b as 'Hida–Tilouine from proposed AC L0c'.

nodes.title: Ordinary p-adic Hermitian modular forms on GU(2,2) and their Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits, G = G_2 = GU(2,2) the unitary similitude group of the skew-Hermitian form w_2 = (0 1_2; −1_2 0) over O_K, and K′ ⊂ G(𝔸^p_f) a neat open compact subgroup. On the ordinary locus of the integral model of the Shimura variety S_G(K′K_p) (with its toroidal and minimal compactifications), and over its Igusa tower, define the space V^q_{a,ord} (dual of the ordinary p-adic Hermitian modular forms; q = 0 for cusp forms, q = 1 for all forms) of weight a with coefficients in Λ_2 = ℤ_p[[Γ_2]], Γ_2 = (1 + pℤ_p)^4 ⊂ T_2(ℤ_p), with the q-expansions at the cusps x = diag(u, t ū^{-1}), the Hecke operators at unramified places, the U_p-operators u_t for t = diag(p^{a_1},…,p^{a_4}), the ordinary projector e = lim u_t^{n!}, and the universal ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ). Specializations at arithmetic weights are classical holomorphic Hermitian modular forms of weight (κ, κ; 0, 0)-type when the weight is sufficiently regular.
hypotheses: p splits in K; K′K_p neat; the p-adic weights are characters of T_2(ℤ_p) through Γ_2 and µ_{p−1}^4.

The Shimura variety, its compactifications, the automorphic bundles and the ordinary Igusa tower are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 (unitary PEL data) and AutomorphicBundles; this node instantiates them for GU(2,2) in SU's normalization.
proofSteps: Instantiate AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4's unitary PEL datum at signature (2,2) and its ordinary forms, using SU §5 conventions (G_n, the Siegel parabolic, cusps C_{n−1}(K)).
Define the ordinary projector by the profinite ordinary projector of PadicFamilies:L0a applied to u_t on the p-adic forms.
q-expansions at x and the Fourier–Jacobi expansions along the Klingen parabolic come from AutomorphicBundles:B5.
acceptance: The degree-one analogue GU(1,1) recovers elliptic modular forms twisted by characters of K, which is how the Eisenstein family is built from a Hida family f.

nodes.title: Hida theory for GU(2,2): freeness, control and the boundary sequence
nodes.statement: For n = 2 and q = 0 (cusp forms) or q = 1 (all forms): (i) V^q_{a,ord} is free of finite rank over Λ_n, and its specializations at finite-order characters ψ of level s have rank independent of ψ and of the weight (SU Thm 6.3.3); (ii) for any Λ_n-algebra A there is a short exact sequence 0 → M^0_{a,ord}(K^p, A) → M^1_{a,ord}(K^p, A) →Φ ⊕_{[g] ∈ C_{n−1}(K)} M^0_{a′,ord}(K^p_{n−1,g}, Λ_{n−1}) ⊗ A → 0, Φ the sum of the Siegel operators to the boundary components (cusp forms on G_{n−1} = GU(1,1)) (SU Thm 6.3.10, from Cor. 5.5.9); (iii) for every sufficiently regular algebraic dominant weight k the canonical surjection h^{S,q}(K^p; Λ_n) ⊗ Λ_n/P_k ↠ h^{S,q}_{k,ord}(K) has nilpotent kernel, so every ℚ̄_p-valued character of the Λ-adic Hecke algebra at P_k comes from a classical ordinary eigenform of weight k (SU Thm 6.4.1). Consequently h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ) is finite over Λ_2 and its arithmetic points of regular weight are Zariski dense.
hypotheses: Weights sufficiently regular in the sense of SU 6.2; neat level; p split in K.
proofSteps: Freeness from vertical control on the Igusa tower (SU §6.2–6.3, Props 6.2.5, Cor. 6.2.6, Thm 6.2.10).
Boundary exact sequence: the Siegel operator surjects onto boundary ordinary forms (SU Cor. 5.5.9, Thm 6.3.10).
Control of the Hecke algebra in sufficiently regular weight (nilpotent kernel, SU Thm 6.4.1); density of such weights in Spec Λ_2.
acceptance: The boundary sequence is what lets one subtract an Eisenstein family from a lift and obtain a cusp form congruent to it.

nodes.title: The p-adic Eisenstein datum and its Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: A p-adic Eisenstein datum D = (A, 𝕀, 𝐟, ψ, ξ, Σ) consists of the ring of integers A of a finite extension of ℚ_p containing ℤ[µ_{M_D p}, i, D_K^{1/2}], a normal domain 𝕀 finite over Λ_{W,A}, an 𝕀-adic ordinary eigenform 𝐟 of tame level M, finite idele class characters ψ and ξ of 𝔸_K^× (ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟), and a finite set of primes Σ containing those dividing M p D_K and the ramification of ξ. Put Λ_D = 𝕀[[Γ^-_K × Γ_K]], a finite local reduced Λ_2-algebra via α ⊗ β (SU 6.5.1), the characters σ_ψ, σ_ξ, σ_{ξ′} = σ_ξσ^c_ξ, and the semisimple representation ρ_D = σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^c_ψε^{-3} ⊕ (ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^{-c}_ξσ^c_ψε^{-2}) ⊕ σ_{χ̄_f,0}ε^{-1}det ρ_𝐟 σ^{-1}_{ξ′}σ^c_ψ of G_K over Frac Λ_D (6.5.2.a). The Eisenstein ideal I_D ⊆ h_D = h_{Σ,0}(K′; Λ_D) is generated by the coefficients of Q_v(X) − Q_{v,D}(X) (v ∉ Σ), the relations u_t − ∏β_i^{a_i} for the U_p-operators with the prescribed (β_1,…,β_4), and the central operators Z_{ℓ,0}, Z^{(i)}_{ℓ,0} minus their values on the Eisenstein characters; E_D ⊆ Λ_D is the kernel of Λ_D → h_D/I_D, so Λ_D/E_D ≅ h_D/I_D (6.5.3.a), and 𝕋_D is the localization of h_D at the maximal ideal containing I_D. The two p-adic L-functions attached to D are L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] (L1/su-padic-l-function) and L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}, the image of the Kubota–Leopoldt function of the Dirichlet character χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′; their product is L_D.
hypotheses: ψ exists with ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟 and unramified outside Σ (SU Thm 12.3.1 hypothesis); (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 when 𝕋_D is used.
proofSteps: Define Λ_D, the characters and ρ_D as in SU 6.5.1–6.5.2.
Instantiate L0/eisenstein-ideal with the Hecke operators listed in SU 6.5.3 and the eigensystem of ρ_D and the U_p-characters.
acceptance: The specialization of ρ_D at an arithmetic point with an associated Eisenstein series is the Galois representation of that Eisenstein series (SU remark after (6.5.2.a)).

nodes.title: Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(2,2) as pullbacks of Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3)
nodes.statement: For a cuspidal eigenform f on GU(1,1) (from an elliptic newform and a character ψ), a character ξ of 𝔸_K^× and a choice of local sections at the places of Σ and at p, construct the holomorphic Klingen-type Eisenstein series E(Z, x; F) on GU(2,2), induced from the Klingen parabolic with Levi GU(1,1) × Res_{K/ℚ}𝔾_m, of weight κ > 6 (SU §9, 'good Eisenstein series' Prop. 9.3.3), its Hecke eigenvalues and Satake parameters (SU §9.5–9.6), and its expression through the pullback of a Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3) along GU(2,2) × GU(1,1) ↪ GU(3,3) paired against f (SU §11, Prop. 11.2.3). The local sections at p and at Σ are chosen as in SU §11.4, so that the Fourier coefficients c(β, x) are products of local Whittaker integrals with explicit values (SU Cor. 11.7.5–11.7.6, §11.8), the singular ones (det β = 0) being multiples of the L-values L^Σ_K(f, χ̄_fξ, κ − 1)·L^Σ(χ̄_fξ̄′, κ − 2).
hypotheses: κ > 6 for the absolutely convergent range; the sections at p have conductor dividing p as in (12.4.2.a) when the family is formed.
The doubling/pullback formalism, the Siegel Eisenstein series on unitary groups and the local doubling integrals are imported; this node owns the Klingen-specific choices and coefficient formulas.
proofSteps: Pullback (doubling) formula: restricting E^{Sieg}_{GU(3,3)} to GU(2,2) × GU(1,1) and integrating against f gives the Klingen series times the standard L-value (SU Prop. 11.2.3, from Shimura/Garrett).
Local computations at unramified places, at Σ and at p (SU §11.4, Props 11.4.13, 11.4.17, 11.4.18, 11.4.23) and the Fourier coefficients (SU §11.6–11.7).
Hecke eigenvalues: E is an eigenform with Hecke polynomial Q_{v,D} (SU §9.5–9.6).
acceptance: The constant terms (Siegel operator images) and all singular Fourier coefficients are divisible by the product of the two L-values; the nonsingular ones are not in general.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban three-variable p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let A, 𝕀, 𝐟, ξ and Σ be as in a p-adic Eisenstein datum, and suppose there is a finite A-valued idele class character ψ with ψ|_{𝔸^×} = χ_𝐟, unramified outside Σ. (i) There is L̃^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ Frac(𝕀) ⊗_𝕀 𝕀_K whose value at every φ ∈ X_{𝕀_K,A}(𝐟, ψ, ξ) is the Petersson-normalized algebraic part of L^Σ_K(f_φ, χ̄_{f_φ}ξ_φ, κ_φ − 1) (SU Thm 12.3.1(i)); (ii) under (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 there is L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} ∈ 𝕀_K whose value at φ is u_{f_φ} times the same L-value normalized by the canonical periods Ω^+_{f_φ}Ω^-_{f_φ}, u_{f_φ} a p-adic unit (SU Thm 12.3.1(ii)). (iii) If moreover χ_𝐟 = 1, ξ = ξ̄^c with conductor dividing (p), (M, D_K) = 1, M = M^+M^- with M^- squarefree with an odd number of primes, all inert in K, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | M^-, then L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} lies in no prime of 𝕀[[Γ_K]] of the form Q·𝕀[[Γ_K]] with Q a height-one prime of 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]] (SU Prop. 12.3.6, from Vatsal's µ = 0).
hypotheses: As stated; the interpolation set X_{𝕀_K,A}(𝐟, ψ, ξ) is defined in SU §12.3 (conductor conditions at p).
proofSteps: Apply the interpolation lemma 12.2.7 to the family g = f^{(1)}_{D,1/M,1} of Prop. 12.2.5; Cor. 11.7.5 identifies the specializations (proof of SU Thm 12.3.1).
Density of X′_D and independence of φ|_{Γ^-_K} place L̃ in Frac(𝕀) ⊗ 𝕀_K; the integral version N_g of Lemma 12.2.7(ii) gives (ii) (L0/canonical-period-congruence-number).

(iii): expand in γ^- − 1; the anticyclotomic specialization at a weight-two point has µ = 0 by Vatsal (through AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/finis-divisibility), so some coefficient is a unit and the series lies in no prime pulled back from 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]].
acceptance: Integrality (ii) requires (irred) and (dist); without them only (i) holds.
The interpolation uses the canonical periods Ω^±; the anticyclotomic restriction is compared with Bertolini–Darmon's function only up to a unit (SU 3.6.14).

sources.match: The two interpolation statements and the non-divisibility by pulled-back height-one primes from Vatsal's theorem.

nodes.title: The Λ_D-adic Klingen Eisenstein family and its constant terms
nodes.statement: Let D be a p-adic Eisenstein datum with cond(ψ_p), cond(ξ_p) | p, (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and K′ ⊆ K′_D with K′K_p neat. (i) There is E_D ∈ M^{a,ord}(K′; Λ_D) whose specialization at every φ ∈ X″_D is u_φ·G_{D_φ}/(Ω^+_{f_φ}Ω^-_{f_φ}) with |u_φ|_p = 1, G_{D_φ} the classical Klingen Eisenstein series (SU Thm 12.4.2(i), Thm 12.4.1); (ii) for x with x_p ∈ Q(ℤ_p) and det β = 0, the β-Fourier coefficient c_D(β, x) lies in L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}·L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}·Λ_D (Thm 12.4.2(ii)); (iii) h ∈ h_D acts on E_D by a homomorphism λ_D: h_D → Λ_D with λ_D(I_D) = 0 (SU 6.5.3). Consequently, if P ⊂ Λ_D is a height-one prime with E_D ≢ 0 modulo P, then ord_P(E_D) ≥ ord_P(L_D) (SU Thm 6.5.4): subtracting a lift of E_D's constant terms produces a cuspidal family congruent to E_D modulo L_D.
hypotheses: (irred)_𝐟, (dist)_𝐟; A satisfies the hypotheses of SU Prop. 12.2.5; conductor condition (12.4.2.a) at p.
The conclusion of Thm 6.5.4 is conditional on E_D being nonzero modulo P; L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality supplies this.
proofSteps: Interpolate each q-expansion coefficient by Lemma 12.2.7 applied to f^{(2)}_{D,β,x} (proof of SU Thm 12.4.1), using Cor. 11.7.6.
Assemble a Λ_D-adic ordinary form by the q-expansion principle and Hida theory (L1/gu22-hida-control).

Thm 6.5.4: if ord_P(L_D) = r and E_D ≢ 0 mod P, the boundary exact sequence lets one subtract a Λ_D-adic lift of E_D's boundary values times L_D^{-1}·(unit), producing a cusp form H ≡ E_D mod P^r, whence 𝕋_D/I_D surjects onto Λ_D/(E_D, P^r).
acceptance: The congruence is with the whole family E_D, not with an individual Eisenstein series; an interpolation formula for E_D alone does not give it.
Excluded case: if E_D ≡ 0 mod P no bound is claimed.

nodes.title: A nonsingular Fourier coefficient is prime to the p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let A be the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p, 𝕀 a domain finite over Λ_{W,A}, 𝐟 ∈ M^{ord}(M, 1; 𝕀) an 𝕀-adic newform with (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and Σ_0 ⊇ {ℓ | pMD_K}. There is a finite Σ ⊇ Σ_0 such that for D = (A, 𝕀, 𝐟, 1, 1, Σ) the set C_D of nonsingular coefficients c_D(β_i, x) of E_D satisfies: (i) every height-one prime of Λ_D containing C_D is of the form PΛ_D with P a height-one prime of 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]]; (ii) if M = M^+M^- with M^- squarefree with an odd number of prime factors, all inert in K, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | M^-, then no height-one prime of Λ_D contains both L^Σ_{𝐟,K,1} and C_D (SU Prop. 13.4.1).
hypotheses: The hypotheses of SU Prop. 12.2.5 on A; the auxiliary primes of Prop. 13.2.5 (a set of primes split in K not dividing the level) are part of the choice of Σ.
proofSteps: Express a Λ_D-combination of the c_D(β_i, x) as a product of Hecke L-values attached to auxiliary CM forms (SU §13.2–13.3, Props 13.2.5, 13.3.4).

Apply the mod-p nonvanishing results of Vatsal and Finis for anticyclotomic twists (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/finis-divisibility, mod-p-nonvanishing) to show that combination is not divisible by any height-one prime other than those pulled back from 𝕀[[Γ^+_K]].
Combine with L1/su-padic-l-function (iii), which excludes the pulled-back primes from L^Σ_{𝐟,K,1}, to get (ii).
acceptance: This is what makes E_D nonzero modulo every height-one prime dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}, so that Thm 6.5.4 applies at those primes.

nodes.title: The four-dimensional pseudo-character of the ordinary GU(2,2) Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For a neat K = K^0_pK^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f) and a finite set S of primes containing p and the primes where K_ℓ is not hyperspecial, there is a pseudo-representation T^S_{K^p}: G_K → h_{S,0}(K^p) of dimension four such that tr R_p(π) = λ^{ord}_π ∘ T^S_{K^p} for every p-ordinary cuspidal π of weight k with π_f^{K^p} ≠ 0 (SU Prop. 7.2.1), where R_p(π) is the four-dimensional Galois representation attached to π (imported from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII: polarized, unramified outside S, crystalline at p when π_p is unramified, with the ordinary filtration at the primes above p). For a datum D, T_D is its composite with h_D, R_D the semisimple representation over the total fraction ring of h_D with trace T_D, and for each irreducible component J, R_J is either absolutely irreducible or, over a finite extension of Frac J, R_1 ⊕ R_2 with two-dimensional R_i satisfying R_i^c ≅ R_i^∨ ⊗ ε^{-3}ω^{1+c}_{K′} (SU Thm 7.3.1).
hypotheses: k regular for the attachment of R_p(π) (SU Thm 7.1.1, from Morel and Shin as explained in Skinner 2010); (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟 for Thm 7.3.1.
The Galois representations of cuspidal representations of GU(2,2) and their local–global compatibility at p are imported (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/6), not constructed here.
proofSteps: Define T(frob_v) := T_v (the Hecke operator giving −1 times the X^3-coefficient of the Hecke polynomial) for v ∉ S ∪ {p}, extend by continuity using Chebotarev density and compactness of h, and check independence of the approximating sequence on a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points (proof of SU Prop. 7.2.1).
The pseudo-representation identities hold because they hold at each classical point and these are dense.

Thm 7.3.1: if R_J were a sum of two characters and an irreducible two-dimensional piece, specialize at a regular-weight point unramified at p to get a CAP representation, excluded by the residual shape tr ρ̄_D; otherwise R_J = R_1 ⊕ R_2 with the stated polarization.
acceptance: The residual pseudo-character of 𝕋_D is tr ρ̄_D: two characters and one irreducible two-dimensional constituent.

nodes.title: The Skinner–Urban Selmer lower bound from the Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: Assume (irred)_𝐟, (dist)_𝐟 and 𝕀 integrally closed. Let T = (T_𝐟 ⊗_𝕀 𝕀[[Γ_K]])(det ρ_𝐟^{-1}σ^{-c}_ξε^{-c}_K) with its ordinary summand T^+, and Ch^Σ_K(ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K) ⊆ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] the characteristic ideal of X^Σ_K(T, T^+). For a height-one prime P_0 ⊂ 𝕀[[Γ_K]] with P = P_0Λ_D such that the four G_{K,p}-characters of SU (7.3.3.a) are residually distinct modulo P: (i) if ord_P(L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}) = 0 then ord_{P_0}(Ch^Σ_K(ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K)) ≥ ord_P(E_D) (SU Thm 7.3.3); (ii) if E_D ≢ 0 modulo P and ord_P(L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}) ≥ 1, then ord_P(Ch^Σ_K) ≥ 1, and if moreover ord_P(L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′}) = 0 then ord_P(Ch^Σ_K) ≥ ord_P(L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ}) (SU Thm 7.3.5).
hypotheses: Residual disjointness (7.3.3.a) is verified in the proof of Thm 7.3.5: the four characters δ²_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}ε_Wε, δ_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}σ_ξε_W, δ_fσ^{-1}_{χ_f}σ^c_ξε_W, σ_{χ_f}ε^{-1}_Wσ^{-1}_{ξ′}ε are not ≡ 1 modulo P, by (dist)_𝐟 and a codimension count.
proofSteps: Set up the lattice datum of SU 7.3.2: A_0 = Λ_D, A = Λ̂_{D,P}, J_0 = E_D, R_0 = 𝕋_D, I_0 = I_D, V_0 = T_𝐟 ⊗ Λ_D, ρ_0 = ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_{χ̄_f,0}σ^{-c}_ξσ^c_ψε^{-2}, V^±_0 from T^+_𝐟, χ, χ′, ν, and σ from R_D.
Apply L0/lattice-construction (Prop. 4.5.6 and Cor. 4.5.7) and Shapiro (L0/sigma-primitive-selmer) to pass from ρ_0 ⊗ χ^{-1} over Λ_D to ρ_𝐟 ⊗ σ_ξε_K over 𝕀[[Γ_K]].
Thm 7.3.5 combines (i) with L1/padic-eisenstein-family (Thm 6.5.4) and checks (7.3.3.a).
acceptance: The bound is height-one-prime by height-one-prime and needs E_D ≢ 0 mod P; L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality supplies this at every P dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}.

nodes.title: Skinner–Urban's two-variable divisibility over K
nodes.statement: Let L ⊆ ℚ̄_p be a finite extension of ℚ_p containing ℚ[µ_{Np}, i, D_K^{1/2}], 𝕀 a normal domain finite over Λ_{W,O_L}, and 𝐟 an 𝕀-adic ordinary eigenform of tame level N with χ_𝐟 = 1. Suppose N = N^+N^- with N^+ divisible only by primes split in K and N^- only by primes inert in K, N^- squarefree with an odd number of prime factors, (irred)_𝐟 and (dist)_𝐟, and ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at every ℓ | N^-. For every finite Σ containing the primes dividing ND_K, Ch^Σ_{K_∞}(𝐟) ⊆ (L^Σ_{𝐟,K}) (SU Thm 3.6.1). For a classical p-ordinary eigenform f ∈ S_k(Np^r, χ; L), k ≥ 2, with χ = ω^{k−2}χ_1 (χ_1 of p-power order and conductor) and the same hypotheses, Ch^Σ_{K_∞,L}(f) ⊆ (L^Σ_{f,K}) (SU Cor. 3.6.2).
hypotheses: As stated; the hypotheses on N^- and ρ̄_𝐟|_{I_ℓ} enter through Vatsal's theorem (L1/su-padic-l-function (iii)); χ_𝐟 = 1 enters there and in the Galois argument; Σ ⊇ primes dividing ND_K avoids local–global compatibility away from p (SU remarks (i)–(v) after Thm 3.6.1).
proofSteps: For each height-one prime P_0 of 𝕀[[Γ_K]] dividing L^Σ_{𝐟,K}, choose the datum of L1/nonsingular-coefficient-coprimality so that E_D ≢ 0 mod P = P_0Λ_D.

If ord_P L^Σ_{χ̄_𝐟ξ̄′} = 0 apply L1/su-selmer-lower-bound (ii); the Dirichlet factor is a unit at P because it lives in the cyclotomic variable only and P_0 is not pulled back (L1/su-padic-l-function (iii)).
Conclude ord_{P_0}(Ch^Σ) ≥ ord_{P_0}(L^Σ_{𝐟,K}) for every height-one P_0, hence the divisorial containment (end of SU §7, p. 108).
Cor. 3.6.2: specialize along 𝕀 → O_L using (3.3.12.b), L0/selmer-specialization-control (ii) and the comparison of L^Σ_{𝐟,K} with L^Σ_{f,K} (SU 3.4.6).
acceptance: Oriented: the characteristic ideal is contained in the ideal of the p-adic L-function (L divides the characteristic power series).
Integral, not after inverting p, under the stated hypotheses.

nodes.title: Skinner–Urban's cyclotomic divisibility
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Np^r, χ; L), k ≥ 2, be a p-ordinary cuspidal eigenform with (irred) and (dist) for ρ_f, χ = ω^{k−2}χ_1 with χ_1 of p-power order and conductor, and a prime q ≠ p with q ∥ N at which ρ̄_f is ramified; choose an imaginary quadratic K in which p splits, every prime dividing N/q splits and q is inert, so N^- = q. Then for every finite set of primes Σ, Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞,L}(f)·Ch^Σ_{ℚ_∞,L}(f ⊗ χ_K) ⊆ (L^Σ_f·L^Σ_{f⊗χ_K}) (SU Cor. 3.6.3). This is the reverse divisibility exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/su-ordinary-theorem, in the normalization of the Σ-imprimitive ordinary Selmer dual and the canonical-period p-adic L-function; the equality (SU Thm 3.6.4, with Kato) is assembled there, not here.
hypotheses: As stated; the integral containment needs only these hypotheses. The integral equality additionally uses Kato's image condition (a basis with image containing SL₂(ℤ_p)), owned by the consumer.

The identification with ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0's ordinary Selmer dual and canonical-period p-adic L-function is made in that roadmap's range (trivial character, p ∤ N, the range of SU Thm 3.6.4); outside it the statement is about SU's own Σ-primitive Selmer group and L^Σ_f.

nodes.title: The semi-ordinary weight space and projector for GU(3,1)
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with p = v_0v̄_0 split, and GU(3,1) the unitary similitude group of signature (3,1), so that GU(3,1)(ℚ_p) ≅ GL_4(ℚ_p) × ℚ_p^× and the diagonal torus of the p-adic group gives a three-dimensional p-adic weight space of characters (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1). The semi-ordinary torus T_so(ℤ_p) ⊂ T(ℤ_p) is the two-dimensional subtorus of weights (0, 0, t^+; t^-), with Iwasawa algebra Λ_so = ℤ_p[[T_so(ℤ_p)]]. On the p-adic forms V on the Igusa tower put U_p := U^+_{p,2}U^+_{p,3}U^-_{p,1}; for every f ∈ V the limit e_so f := lim_{r→∞} U_p^{r!} f exists and defines the semi-ordinary projector e_so. A classical form is semi-ordinary if it is fixed by e_so; this asks unit U_p-eigenvalues only in the two directions of T_so, so it allows forms whose GL_2 part at p is not ordinary (a_p = 0 is allowed).
hypotheses: p ≥ 3 split in K; the operators U^±_{p,i} are those of CLW (3.0.7)–(3.0.8) on p-integral forms.
The convergence of U_p^{r!} on every f uses the finiteness property (F) of CLW Thm 4.6.1, proved there; the generic profinite projector is imported.
proofSteps: Define U_p and verify property (F) for forms in V^♭ by CLW Prop. 3.0.2 and Prop. 4.5.2, and for all of V by Prop. 4.5.3.
Apply the profinite ordinary projector of PadicFamilies:L0a to the locally finite endomorphism U_p to obtain e_so.
acceptance: Semi-ordinary is weaker than ordinary: an ordinary form is semi-ordinary, while a form whose GL_2 constituent at p has a_p = 0 can be semi-ordinary and is killed by the ordinary projector.

nodes.title: Semi-ordinary Hida theory and the fundamental exact sequence
nodes.statement: With e_so as in L2s/semi-ordinary-weight-space: (1) the duals V^{0,*}_so = Hom(e_so V^0, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) and V^*_so = Hom(e_so V, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) are free of finite rank over Λ_so (vertical control, CLW Thm 3.0.7 for cusp forms, Thm 4.6.1 for all forms); (2) the spaces of Λ_so-families of tame level K^p_f, M^0_so = Hom_{Λ_so}(V^{0,*}_so, Λ_so) and M_so = Hom_{Λ_so}(V^*_so, Λ_so), specialize isomorphically at every weight (τ^+, τ^-) with 0 ≥ t^+ ≥ −t^- + 4 onto the limits of e_so-parts of mod p^m forms of that weight, and classical semi-ordinary forms embed into the specialization after inverting p (CLW (2.9.1)); (3) there is a fundamental exact sequence 0 → M^0_{so} → M_{so} → ⊕_{g ∈ C(K^p_f)} M_{GU(2)}(K^p_{f,g}K_{p,0}, Ô^{ur}_L) ⊗ ℤ_p[[Γ_K]] → 0 given by the Siegel operators Φ_g at the cusp labels g, after specializing the family along the character ξ (CLW Thm 2.9.1, used in Thm 8.1.1).
hypotheses: The weights in (2) satisfy 0 ≥ t^+ ≥ −t^- + 4; for the Klingen family, 0 ≫ t^+ ≫ −t^-.
The Shimura variety of GU(3,1), its toroidal and minimal compactifications, the Igusa tower and the boundary strata are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 and AutomorphicBundles.
proofSteps: Base change and q-expansion: CLW Props 3.0.1–3.0.6; vertical control for cusp forms (Thm 3.0.7).

The boundary: restriction to the strata Z_{g,n} gives the exact sequences (4.4.2)–(4.4.3) with the Siegel operators Φ_g (Prop. 4.4.1), whose global sections are forms on the zero-dimensional Shimura variety of GU(2).
Finiteness (F) and the vertical control for all forms (Props 4.5.1–4.5.3, Thm 4.6.1); combine into Thm 2.9.1.
acceptance: The exactness on the right is what allows a Λ_so-adic lift of the boundary values of the Klingen family, hence a cuspidal family congruent to it.

nodes.title: The semi-ordinary Klingen Eisenstein family on GU(3,1)
nodes.statement: Let π be generated by a weight-two newform f satisfying CLW §5.2 (every π_v unramified, Steinberg or an unramified quadratic twist of Steinberg; π_p unramified; a prime q nonsplit in K with π_q ramified, and π ramified at 2 if 2 is nonsplit; ρ̄_π|_{G_K} irreducible), and ξ an algebraic Hecke character of K of ∞-type (0, k_0), k_0 even. Construct a measure E^{Kling}_φ ∈ Meas(Γ_K, e_so V_{GU(3,1),ξ} ⊗̂ Ô^{ur}_L) whose specialization at an algebraic Hecke character τ (with τ_{p-adic} factoring through Γ_K and ξτ of ∞-type (0,k), k ≥ 6 even) is the semi-ordinary projection of the holomorphic Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(3,1) induced from (π_D, ξτ) on the Klingen Levi, built by the doubling method from the p-adic Siegel Eisenstein measure on GU(3,3) (CLW Thm 5.9.1, Thm 5.5.1, Prop. 5.10.1). Its degenerate Fourier–Jacobi coefficients Φ_g(E^{Kling}_φ)(g′) lie in (L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{ξ,ℚ}·L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{π,K,ξ}) ⊆ Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] (CLW Thm 6.1.1), where L_{ξ,ℚ} is the Kubota–Leopoldt function (6.1.1) and L_{π,K,ξ} the Eischen–Wan function with interpolation (6.1.2).
hypotheses: CLW §5.2 hypotheses on π and ξ; the auxiliary primes ℓ, ℓ′ and the sections at Σ ∪ {ℓ, ℓ′} chosen in §§5.6–5.7 using Hsieh's mod-p nonvanishing.

The Siegel Eisenstein measures on unitary groups, the pullback formula and the local doubling integrals are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 and L4e (Eischen–Wan's ordinary U(3,1) family is their r = 2 case); CLW's semi-ordinary sections at p, which replace Eischen–Wan's ordinary ones, and the Klingen choices are owned here.
proofSteps: Choose the definite quaternion algebra D ramified at q and ∞ and the Jacquet–Langlands transfer π_D (CLW §5.4); fix the sections at each place (§§5.6–5.8), with the auxiliary characters of §5.6 chosen by Hsieh's nonvanishing.
Interpolate the Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3) into a measure (Thm 5.9.1) and pull back along GU(3,1) × GU(0,2) ↪ GU(3,3) against π_D (Thm 5.5.1, doubling formula), applying e_so (Prop. 5.10.1).
Compute the constant terms at each cusp label: the Siegel operator images are the L-value products (Thm 6.1.1).
acceptance: Shared local test data: the sections at p and the auxiliary characters are fixed before any arithmetic conclusion, and FW's general-weight family (L2/vector-valued-klingen-family) reuses them.

nodes.title: A Fourier–Jacobi coefficient of the semi-ordinary Klingen family is a unit
nodes.statement: With E^{Kling}_φ as in L2s/semi-ordinary-klingen-family and the auxiliary data of CLW §§5.6, 7.7 (a CM family h, the theta functions θ, θ_3, and operators T_ns, T′_ns at the nonsplit places), the functional obtained by taking the β = 1 Fourier–Jacobi coefficient, pairing with an explicit theta function on the Jacobi group of U(2) and then with h, sends E^{Kling}_φ to an element of Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] that is a unit times a nonzero constant (CLW §7, Props 7.4.2, 7.6.1, 7.7.1, 7.9.1, 7.11.1–7.11.3, 7.12.1). The proof expresses the value through Ichino's triple product formula as a product of p-adic L-functions L_1,…,L_6 of auxiliary CM forms and Rallis inner products, each a unit or a fixed nonzero constant by the choice of auxiliary characters and Hsieh's mod-p nonvanishing and µ = 0 theorems.
hypotheses: Auxiliary characters chosen as in CLW §5.6 so that the relevant anticyclotomic Hecke L-values are nonzero modulo p (Hsieh 2012, 2014).

Ichino's triple product formula for definite U(2) / D^× and the local triple product integrals at nonsplit places are inputs (requested from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3; gap 'ichino-triple-product').
proofSteps: The β-th Fourier–Jacobi coefficient of the Siegel Eisenstein series on GU(3,3) is a finite sum of products of Siegel Eisenstein series on U(2,2) and theta functions on the unitary Jacobi group (CLW Prop. 7.4.2; the Jacobi group and Fourier–Jacobi periods are MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.6's).
Restrict to (N·U(2)) × U(2), pair with θ⋆ and then with h via the doubling formula; the result is a triple product integral ∫ h θ f (Props 7.6.1, 7.7.1).

Ichino's formula and the Rallis inner product formula (Prop. 7.9.1) evaluate it as a product of L-values; local integrals at nonsplit places are nonzero by Prop. 7.12.1; interpolation of each factor (Props 7.11.1–7.11.3) gives the unit statement.
acceptance: The coefficient is a unit, so no height-one prime of Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] contains it; this is what makes the Eisenstein congruence measured by L_{π,K,ξ}L_{ξ,ℚ}.

sources.match: The Fourier–Jacobi computation: Jacobi-group expansion, CM family, Rallis inner products, triple product integrals at nonsplit places.
The five-step pattern: Fourier–Jacobi coefficient of the Siegel series, restriction, pairing with θ⋆ and h, interpolation, Ichino's formula.

nodes.title: The CLW Eisenstein ideal is bounded by the p-adic L-functions
nodes.statement: Let ϕ be as in CLW Prop. 7.11.2 and E_{π,ξ} ⊆ Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] the Eisenstein ideal (L0/eisenstein-ideal) of the semi-ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra 𝕋^0_{so,ξ,Γ_K} for the eigensystem of E^{Kling}_ϕ. For every height-one prime P of Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] with P ∩ Ô^{ur}_L = 0, ord_P(L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{π,K,ξ}·L^{Σ∪{ℓ,ℓ′}}_{ξ,ℚ}) ≤ ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) (CLW Thm 8.1.1).
hypotheses: P not containing p (P ∩ Ô^{ur}_L = 0).
proofSteps: By L2s/semi-ordinary-hida-theory the fundamental exact sequence lets one lift the boundary values of E^{Kling}_ϕ divided by L_{π,K,ξ}L_{ξ,ℚ} modulo P^r to a Λ-adic family.
Subtracting gives a family whose image modulo P^r is cuspidal; it is nonzero because the Fourier–Jacobi coefficient of L2s/fourier-jacobi-primitivity is a unit.
Hence the Hecke eigensystem of E^{Kling} is congruent modulo P^r to a cuspidal one, i.e. 𝕋^0/I surjects onto Λ/(E_{π,ξ}, P^r) with r = ord_P(L·L).
acceptance: The bound is height-one prime by height-one prime and excludes P ∋ p; it is one-sided.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of the GU(3,1) pseudo-character: excluding CAP components
nodes.statement: Let 𝕋 be the semi-ordinary (or ordinary) cuspidal Hecke algebra of GU(3,1) localized at the Eisenstein maximal ideal, T: G_K → 𝕋 its four-dimensional pseudo-character (built as in L1/gu22-galois-pseudocharacter from the Galois representations of cuspidal representations of U(3,1)), and suppose ρ̄_π|_{G_K} is irreducible. Then for every Frac(A)-algebra map λ: 𝕋 ⊗ Frac(A) → K′, the representation σ_λ is absolutely irreducible or contains an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional subrepresentation whose trace is ≡ χ + χ^{-c} modulo I — Wan20's property (9) (CLW proof of Thm 8.2.1). If instead T = δ_1 + δ_2 + δ_3 with δ_3 two-dimensional and residually tr ρ̄_π, then at an arithmetic point x of weight (0,0,t^+;t^-) with 0 ≫ t^+ ≫ −t^-, a twist of the specialization of δ_3 descends to a G_ℚ-representation ρ′_{3,x} which is modular (ordinary case: as in SU Thm 7.3.1; non-ordinary case: ρ_Π|_{G_{K,p}} is crystalline by a Jacquet-module argument and the semi-ordinary slopes, and Kisin's theorem applies; in general weight FW uses Pan's theorem), so Π is CAP, which Harris's Thm 2.5.6 excludes in these weights.
hypotheses: ρ̄_π|_{G_K} irreducible; arithmetic points in the absolutely convergent range of sufficiently regular weight.
The unitary forms and Hecke operators are the AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4 carriers; the semi-ordinary projector is L2s's own, since L4 plans only the ordinary one.
Harris (1984) Thm 2.5.6 (no holomorphic CAP forms of these weights on U(3,1)) is an input not planned in the atlas (gap 'harris-cap').
proofSteps: Suppose the pseudo-character is a sum δ_1 + δ_2 + δ_3; residual irreducibility of ρ̄_π gives a two-dimensional 𝕋-valued representation for δ_3.
Ordinary π: the specialization of δ_3 at x is ordinary and modular by the SU argument.

Non-ordinary π: Edixhoven makes ρ̄_π|_{G_{ℚ_p}} irreducible; Jacquet modules show Π_p is an unramified principal series (the semi-ordinary valuations (8.2.4)–(8.2.5) force distinct ratios ≠ p^{±1}), so ρ_Π|_{G_{K,p}} and ρ′_{3,x} are crystalline; ρ̄′_{3,x} is not induced from ℚ(√p*), so Kisin's modularity lifting applies (FW: Pan's Fontaine–Mazur theorem for de Rham ρ with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} absolutely irreducible).
Modularity of ρ′_{3,x} makes Π CAP (Klingen type), contradicting Harris Thm 2.5.6 for the chosen weights.
acceptance: Shared by L2s/clw-main-divisibility and L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility; the RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/6 addendum asks exactly for these GL₂ modularity and Harris inputs.

The same argument in general weight, with modularity from Pan's Thm 1.0.4.

nodes.title: The Castella–Liu–Wan divisibility over the cyclotomic-localized ring
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic, p ≥ 3 split in K, and π, ξ as in CLW §5.2. Let Γ^+_K ⊂ Γ_K be the rank-one ℤ_p-submodule on which complex conjugation acts by +1 and R := O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] ⊗_{O_L[[Γ^+_K]]} Frac(O_L[[Γ^+_K]]), the localization inverting every nonzero element of the cyclotomic coefficient subring O_L[[Γ^+_K]]. Then, as fractional ideals of R, (L_{π,K,ξ}) ⊇ char_R(X_{π,K,ξ} ⊗_{O_L[[Γ^+_K]]} R), where X_{π,K,ξ} is the dual of the Selmer group of T_{π,K,ξ} = T_π(ε^2_{cyc})|_{G_K}(ξ^{-1}) ⊗ ℤ_p[[Γ_K]](Ψ^{-1}_K) with relaxed condition at one prime above p and unramified condition at the other (CLW Thm 8.2.1(1)). The localization is in the cyclotomic subring; it is not the inversion of p.
hypotheses: CLW §5.2; the excluded height-one primes are exactly those with P ∩ O_L[[Γ^+_K]] ≠ 0 (pulled back from the cyclotomic line) — in particular primes where (X_{ξ∘Nm} ⊗ ℚ)_P ≠ 0 may be among them.
If X_{π,K,ξ} is not torsion its characteristic ideal is 0 and the statement is empty.
proofSteps: Reduce to the Σ ∪ {ℓ,ℓ′}-primitive inclusion (L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison; JSW Thm 6.1.6 and Greenberg–Vatsal Prop. 2.4).

For P with P ∩ O^{ur}_L[[Γ^+_K]] = 0, the inequality ord_P(L) ≤ length(X_P) follows from ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) ≤ length(X_P) by L2s/clw-eisenstein-congruence (L_{ξ,ℚ} lives in the cyclotomic variable, hence is a unit at P).

Set up the lattice datum (1)–(5) with ν trivial, χ = ξΨ_K, ρ from ρ_π, σ the pseudo-representation of the semi-ordinary Hecke algebra, I = E_{π,ξ}A_P; check (6)–(8) as in Wan20 and (9) by L2s/cap-exclusion; apply L0/lattice-construction (Wan20 Prop. 9.2) where ord_P(E_{π,ξ}) > 0 and (X_{ξ∘Nm} ⊗ ℚ)_P = 0.
acceptance: The statement is one-sided and localized; neither torsion of X nor equality is proved here.
Height-one primes pulled back from O_L[[Γ^+_K]] are not controlled: CLW cannot prove the analogue of Wan20 Lemma 9.3 with π fixed.

nodes.title: Integrality of the CLW p-adic L-function and the p-inverted divisibility
nodes.statement: In the setting of L2s/clw-main-divisibility: (a) if ξ_p ≢ ξ_p̄ modulo the maximal ideal of O_L, then L_{π,K,ξ} ∈ O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]]; (b) if moreover ξ|_{𝔸_ℚ^×} = ω² (ω the Teichmüller character) with k_0 ≡ 0 mod 2(p − 1), the local base-change root number ε_v(1/2, BC(π) × ξ_0) equals 1 at every finite place v nonsplit in K, and the conductor of ξ is divisible only by primes split in K, then (L_{π,K,ξ}) ⊇ char_{O^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] ⊗ ℚ}(X_{π,K,ξ} ⊗ ℚ) (CLW Thm 8.2.1(2)): the containment holds after inverting p, without the cyclotomic localization. This is the source-qualified input that RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6a imports for its supersingular branch; it is not a nonordinary equality.
hypotheses: (a) needs residual distinctness ξ_p ≢ ξ_p̄, which gives (irred) and (dist) for the CM form σ_ξ.
(b) adds the four listed conditions; the containment is only after ⊗ ℚ.
proofSteps: (a): as in Wan20 §7E, build L^{Hida}_{π,K,ξ} as the product of Hida's Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function for the ordinary CM family g through σ_ξ and the newform f, and Katz's p-adic L-function on the line interpolating values at 1; only the ordinarity of g is used.

Hida–Tilouine (Thm 7.1, (8.8b)) and Hida's Lemma 5.3(vi) (Petersson norm against the adjoint L-value) show L^{Hida} and L_{π,K,ξ} agree on a dense set of weights, so they are equal; the anticyclotomic main conjecture for CM fields (L0/hida-tilouine-anticyclotomic) under (irred) and (dist) gives integrality of L^{Hida}.

(b): Hsieh's vanishing of the anticyclotomic µ-invariant shows L_{π,K,ξ} lies in no height-one prime pulled back from O_L[[Γ^+_K]] other than possibly (p), so combining with L2s/clw-main-divisibility the excluded primes contribute nothing after inverting p.
acceptance: RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/25: the µ = 0 input is AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h's Theorem B; RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/26: the integrality rests on Hida's Rankin–Selberg family p-adic L-function and the Hida–Tilouine main conjecture, both recorded with their owners.

nodes.title: Semi-ordinary Hida theory on GU(3,1) in general weight
nodes.statement: For f a normalized cuspidal eigenform of even weight k ≥ 2 and the vector-valued semi-ordinary forms on GU(3,1) of weight k = (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1) in the family set X_ρ of Fouquet–Wan: the semi-ordinary parts e_α·V_k(K_0(p,p^n)) are p-divisible with uniformly bounded classical dimensions (Props 7.9–7.10); for each weight k = (a_1, a_2, a_3; b_1) ∈ X_ρ there is A(a) such that, for b_1 large compared with A(a), the restriction e_α M_k(K_0(p), O) ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p → e_α·V_k(K_0(p)) is an isomorphism (FW Thm 7.11); for q = 0 or ∅ the Λ̃-adic families V^q_so are free of finite rank and M^q_so(K, Λ̃) ⊗ Λ̃/P_k ≅ e_α M^q_k(K, O) at such weights (Thm 7.12), with Thm 7.15 and the weight-k boundary sequence of Thm 7.17; and the short sequence of cusp forms, forms and boundary forms is exact (Thm 7.18). These extend L2s/semi-ordinary-hida-theory (CLW, weight two) to general weight and are the only new Hida-theoretic input L2 owns.

nodes.title: The vector-valued Klingen Eisenstein family and the Greenberg p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let π = π_f be the unitary automorphic representation of a weight-k form f and Σ a finite set containing the bad primes. (i) There is L^Σ_{f,K,ξ_0} ∈ Λ_{K,O^{ur}} ⊗ ℚ_p interpolating, at characters ξ_φ of Γ_K that are avatars of Hecke characters of conductor p and infinity type (κ_φ/2 + m_φ, −κ_φ/2 − m_φ) with κ_φ ≥ 6 even and m_φ ≥ (k−2)/2, the values L^Σ(π̃, ξ_φ, (κ_φ − 1)/2) times the stated periods and local factors (FW Prop. 7.19(i), from Eischen–Wan Thm 1.2); (ii) there is a family of formal q-expansions E_{f,ξ_0} whose specializations at a Zariski-dense set of arithmetic points are the Fourier–Jacobi expansions of the highest weight vectors of the holomorphic vector-valued Klingen Eisenstein series on GU(3,1) built by the pullback formula, eigen for U_{t+} with nonzero eigenvalue (Prop. 7.19(ii)); (iii) the constant terms a_{t,[g]}(0) are divisible by L^Σ_{f,K,ξ_0}·L^Σ_{τ̄′} (Prop. 7.19(iii)). After the reparametrization t^{-c}_{ξ′_0}, L^{Gr,Σ}_{f,K} := t^{-c}_{ξ′_0}(L_{f,K,ξ_0}) is the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function, it equals L^{Hida}_{f⊗g}·L^{Katz}_K·h_K (FW Cor. 7.21, L2/greenberg-function-factorization) and lies in O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] (FW Lemma 7.22).
hypotheses: Eischen–Wan's distinct-Satake-parameter assumption is unnecessary in the U(2) case (FW remark after Prop. 7.19).
The Klingen family of Eischen–Wan (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4e) is the analytic carrier; FW's reparametrization, the Ikeda-type archimedean factorization and the integrality are owned here.
proofSteps: Translate Eischen–Wan Thm 1.2 to the semi-ordinary GU(3,1) setting with the shared local data of L2s/semi-ordinary-klingen-family (FW Prop. 7.19).
Reparametrize by t^{-c}_{ξ′_0} (γ′ ↦ γ′ξ′_0(γ′)^{-1}, then γ′ ↦ γ′^{-c}).

Integrality (Lemma 7.22): the denominators are powers of p times finitely many Euler factors, while Wan's argument bounds them by powers of the CM-family variable; the two sets are disjoint, so the denominator is a unit.
acceptance: Only the vector-valued, general-weight construction is new here; the weight-two scalar family is L2s's.

nodes.title: Factorization of the Greenberg function into Hida and Katz factors
nodes.statement: With the normalizations of FW §4.5.2 and Appendix B, the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function of f over K factors as L^{Gr}_K(f) = L^{Hida}_{f⊗g}·L^{Katz}_K·h_K, where L^{Hida}_{f⊗g} is Hida's Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function of f against the canonical CM Hida family g, L^{Katz}_K is Katz's p-adic L-function of K restricted to the relevant line and h_K the class number factor (FW Cor. 7.21, with Prop. 4.35 for the Katz normalization). The factorization is an identity in Frac(O^{ur}[[Γ_K]]) obtained by comparing interpolation formulas on a Zariski-dense set; it carries the class-number, period and local factors explicitly and is not routed to L5a.

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan Fourier–Jacobi coefficient and the Eisenstein ideal bound
nodes.statement: For the Klingen family E^{Kling} of L2/vector-valued-klingen-family and the functional FJ_{h,β,θ⋆}(E) = ⟨e^{ord} l_{θ⋆}(FJ_β(E)), h⟩, the value FJ_{h,β,θ⋆}(E^{Kling}) is the product of an element of O^{ur}[[Γ_K]]^× and an element of ℚ̄_p^× (FW Prop. 7.29). Consequently, for the Eisenstein ideal E_D of the reduced semi-ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra 𝕋_D (FW Def. 7.30, L0/eisenstein-ideal) and every height-one prime P ≠ (p) of O^{ur}[[Γ_K]], ord_P(L^{Gr,Σ}_{f,K}) ≤ ord_P(E_D) (FW Lemma 7.31).

Ichino's formula evaluates the resulting triple product as L_3L_4 times Rallis inner products (interpolated by L_3, L_4) and local integrals; the ratio to L_1L_2L_5L_6 is a fixed nonzero constant (FW Prop. 7.29).
Lemma 7.31 follows as in Wan20 Lemma 9.1, with Prop. 7.29 and Thm 7.18 in place of the weight-two inputs.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's GU(3,1) divisibility for the Greenberg main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized cuspidal eigenform of even weight k, trivial character and conductor N prime to p, such that either ρ̄_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is absolutely irreducible or f is ordinary at p; suppose every prime q | N nonsplit in K satisfies q ∥ N and there is at least one such q, that 2 ∥ N if 2 is nonsplit in K, and that ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible over G_K. Then char_{O^{ur}[[Γ_K]]}(X^{Gr}_K(f) ⊗_O O^{ur}) ⊆ (L^{Gr}_K(f)) up to height-one primes pulled back from O[[Γ^+]]; if moreover every ℓ | N nonsplit in K is ramified in K with π_ℓ the Steinberg representation twisted by the unramified character sending ℓ to (−1)^{ℓ^{k/2−1}}, the whole containment holds (FW Thm 7.32 = Thm 4.41 = Thm 1.12). Here X^{Gr}_K(f) is the dual of the Greenberg Rankin–Selberg Selmer group (FW Def. 4.39: Greenberg condition at v_0, strict at v̄_0, unramified-quotient conditions away from p).
hypotheses: As stated; ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} crystalline in Thm 4.41's form.
The first containment excludes height-one primes pulled back from O[[Γ^+]]; the second needs the Steinberg-twist hypothesis to invoke the anticyclotomic µ = 0 theorem.
proofSteps: Σ-primitive version first: lattice construction (Wan20 Prop. 9.2; L0/lattice-construction) shows that E_D contains the characteristic ideal of the dual Selmer group, with Wan20's condition (9) by L2s/cap-exclusion (modularity from Pan's theorem in general weight).
Lemma 7.31 (L2/fw-fourier-jacobi-unit) bounds ord_P(L^{Gr,Σ}) ≤ ord_P(E_D) for P ≠ (p).
Put back the Euler factors at Σ (Greenberg–Vatsal Prop. 2.4; K_∞ contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension; L0/primitive-imprimitive-comparison).

Under the Steinberg hypothesis apply Hsieh's anticyclotomic µ = 0 to see that L^{Gr}_K(f) lies in no height-one prime of O[[Γ^+]], hence is prime to the Dirichlet factor in the constant terms (L2/exceptional-height-one-primes).
acceptance: One-sided; RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/24 is answered by importing CLW's weight-two Hida theory and the lattice argument from L2s and L0.

nodes.title: Removing the excluded height-one primes
nodes.statement: Let L ∈ O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] be L^{Gr}_K(f) (or Wan's L_{f,K,ξ}). If the anticyclotomic restriction of L has vanishing µ-invariant — which holds when every prime ℓ | N nonsplit in K is ramified in K with π_ℓ the appropriately twisted Steinberg representation and the residual and conductor hypotheses of Hsieh's Theorem B are met — then L lies in no height-one prime of O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] of the form Q·O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] with Q a height-one prime of O[[Γ^+]]; hence it is prime to the cyclotomic Dirichlet factor L^Σ_{τ̄′} of the constant terms, and a divisibility proved up to pulled-back primes holds integrally. For a Hida family, Wan20 Lemma 9.3 gives the same conclusion; for a single form outside the µ = 0 range the exceptional primes remain excluded.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3h/theorem-b (Hsieh's µ = 0) for the anticyclotomic specialization; the auxiliary-field choice of L2/auxiliary-field-selection must preserve them (no nonsplit-prime or minimality condition dropped).
proofSteps: Write L = Σ a_i (γ^- − 1)^i with a_i ∈ O^{ur}[[Γ^+]]; L ∈ Q·O^{ur}[[Γ_K]] iff every a_i ∈ Q.

Specialize at the trivial character of Γ^+ (or at a weight point): the anticyclotomic function has µ = 0, so some a_i is a unit there, so not all a_i lie in Q (the argument of SU Prop. 12.3.6, with Hsieh in place of Vatsal).
The Dirichlet factor lives in the cyclotomic variable, so it is a product of pulled-back primes and is coprime to L.
acceptance: Test: an excluded height-one prime pulled back from O[[Γ^+]] at which the Dirichlet factor vanishes is not claimed for L unless the µ = 0 hypothesis holds.

nodes.title: Choosing the auxiliary imaginary quadratic field for the Fouquet–Wan route
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)), p ∤ N, k ≥ 2 even, satisfy the hypotheses of FW Thm 1.6 (ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible; some ℓ ∥ N with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ}_f = 1 and dim ρ̄^{G_ℓ}_f = 0; ordinary with χ̄_1 ≠ χ̄_2). Then there is an imaginary quadratic K with p split, the chosen ℓ inert in K (so ℓ is a nonsplit prime with ℓ ∥ N), every other prime dividing N split in K, 2 split or ramified-Steinberg as required, and ρ̄_f|_{G_K} absolutely irreducible; for such K all hypotheses of L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility (first containment) and of L2/castella-wan-equivalence hold, and no nonsplit-prime or minimality condition is dropped in passing from f to f over K.

proofSteps: Impose local splitting conditions at p, ℓ and the primes of N by choosing D_K in finitely many residue classes; infinitely many such K exist.
Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄_f|_{G_K}: ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible over ℚ, so it fails over K only if ρ̄_f is induced from K; this excludes at most finitely many K.
Check each hypothesis of Thm 7.32 and of the Castella–Wan comparison: q = ℓ is nonsplit with q ∥ N; all nonsplit primes are q ∥ N; ρ̄_f|_{G_K} irreducible; ordinary at p.
acceptance: The Steinberg-twist hypothesis of the second containment is not automatic; when it fails the exceptional primes are handled by L2/exceptional-height-one-primes or remain excluded.

nodes.title: Λ-adic Beilinson–Flach classes for a Hida family and the CM family
nodes.statement: Let 𝐟 be a Hida family with coefficient ring 𝕀 and g the canonical CM Hida family of K (with T_g ≅ Ind^ℚ_K ℤ_p[[Γ_p]]). The Kings–Loeffler–Zerbes Beilinson–Flach class BF_{𝐟,g} ∈ H¹(ℚ, T_𝐟 ⊗̂ T_g ⊗̂ Λ_Γ), obtained from Rankin–Eisenstein classes on products of modular curves (diagonal pushforward of Eisenstein classes, Siegel units) with tame and p-power norm relations, defines through Shapiro's lemma a class BF ∈ H¹(K, T) and, after the twist tw_{Θ^{-1}}, a class BF† ∈ Sel^{Gr,∅}(K, T†) (Greenberg condition at one prime above p, relaxed at the other) over 𝕀[[Γ_K]] (CW Thm 3.6, from KLZ17 Def. 8.1.1 with m = 1 and LLZ14 Lemma 6.8.9 to remove the auxiliary c; membership in the Selmer group by KLZ17 Prop. 8.1.7). Specializations at weight-k points give the classes used in FW §4.4 and §4.8.

nodes.title: Greenberg and Beilinson–Flach main conjectures over K are equivalent
nodes.statement: Let 𝐟 be a Hida family with ρ_𝐟|_{G_K} irreducible. The following are equivalent, up to powers of p: (i) X^{Gr,0}(K_∞, A†_𝐟) is 𝕀[[Γ_K]]-torsion, Sel^{Gr,∅}(K, T†) has rank one, and char(X^{Gr,0}) = char(Sel^{Gr,∅}(K,T†)/𝕀[[Γ_K]]·BF†); (ii) X^{∅,0}(K_∞, A†_𝐟) and Sel^{0,∅}(K, T†) are torsion and char(X^{∅,0})·𝕀^{ur}[[Γ_K]] = (tw_{Θ^{-1}}(L_p(𝐟/K))) (CW Thm 3.8). The same argument holds for a weight-k specialization with the Greenberg main conjecture supplied by L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility in place of the weight-two input (FW §4.8). Each divisibility direction in (ii) corresponds to the same direction in (i).

proofSteps: The two Poitou–Tate four-term exact sequences for the Selmer structures (Gr,∅) ⊃ (Gr,0) and (∅,∅) ⊃ (∅,0) relate the four modules; the Coleman maps of L2/bf-explicit-reciprocity identify the local terms with the p-adic L-functions.
Rank and torsion statements are proved before any cancellation: loc_v(BF†) is non-torsion, so Sel^{Gr,∅} has rank one when X^{Gr,0} is torsion.
Multiplicativity of characteristic ideals along the exact sequences gives the equivalence, with pseudo-null cokernels absorbed.

nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) be a normalized eigencuspform of weight k ≥ 2 with ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} crystalline (p ∤ N) and short, ρ̄_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} absolutely irreducible, and some ℓ ∥ N with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1 and dim ρ̄^{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} = 0. Then Kato's main conjecture holds for M(f): char H²(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw) = char H¹(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw (FW Thm 4.51 = Thm 1.13; Thm 4.38 under the residual hypothesis of Thm 1.7). The proof first gives the equalities of Prop. 4.42 after inverting p (through Pottharst's analytic Iwasawa theory and Selmer complexes over ΛK,∞), then removes the power of p by the unramified local theory along the line through the point (§4.6.3, Prop. 4.48), and treats equal Satake parameters through the Bianchi three-variable p-adic L-function of Betina–Williams (§4.7).
hypotheses: As stated; the distinct-Satake-parameter case first, then §4.7 for the p-irregular case.
Kato's one-sided bound (KatoEulerSystems:L4) supplies the divisibility F_1 | F of the proof of Thm 4.51.
proofSteps: Prop. 4.42: from L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility over K and the Beilinson–Flach reciprocity of L2/bf-explicit-reciprocity in analytic families, via Poitou–Tate for Selmer complexes (FW §4.5, Props 4.28, 4.30, 4.43, Cor. 4.44), get the equality after inverting p.
§4.3: control of Selmer groups and absence of pseudo-null submodules (Prop. 4.20).

§4.6.3: along the unramified line through the point, the integral local subspace of L2/unramified-exponential-boundedness gives the bound at a generic arithmetic point (Prop. 4.48, Lemmas 4.49–4.50); with Kato's divisibility F_1 | F and Kato's explicit reciprocity this gives Thm 4.51.
§4.7: when the Satake parameters coincide, compare with the Betina–Williams Bianchi p-adic L-function (Prop. 4.53).
acceptance: Integral, not only after inverting p; this is the seed FW Prop. 5.6 uses at crystalline-short points of the deformation space.

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan ordinary reverse divisibility (Theorem 1.6 by §4.8)
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)), p ∤ N, k ≥ 2, be an eigencuspform with (1) ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible; (2) some ℓ ∥ N with dim_𝔽 ρ̄^{I_ℓ}_f = 1 and dim_𝔽 ρ̄^{G_ℓ}_f = 0; (3) ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} an extension 0 → χ_1 → ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} → χ_2 → 0 with χ̄_1 ≠ χ̄_2. Then char_{Λ_Iw} H¹(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw divides char_{Λ_Iw} H²(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw) (FW Thm 1.6). The route is FW §4.8, not SU plus a period lemma: over an auxiliary K (L2/auxiliary-field-selection) prove the two-variable Greenberg Rankin–Selberg main conjecture divisibility by L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility, transfer it through L2/castella-wan-equivalence to the Beilinson–Flach formulation, descend to the cyclotomic line, separate the twist factor f ⊗ χ_K, and remove the power of p by a §4.6.3-type integral argument that uses Kato's one-sided bound. No comparison of canonical and Gross periods is used.
hypotheses: Hypotheses (1)–(3) of FW Thm 1.6 exactly; trivial character, even weight for the GU(3,1) input.
FW §4.8 only indicates this argument ('the details are given in Castella–Wan Thm 3.8 ... for weight 2'); the p-power step in the ordinary case is not written out in the source (gap 'fw-4-8-sketch').
proofSteps: Choose K by L2/auxiliary-field-selection; L2/fw-greenberg-divisibility gives char(X^{Gr}) ⊆ (L^{Gr}) up to pulled-back primes, integrally when L2/exceptional-height-one-primes applies.
L2/castella-wan-equivalence (weight k) converts this into the Beilinson–Flach divisibility char(X^{Gr,0}) ⊆ char(Sel^{Gr,∅}/BF†), up to powers of p.
Specialize to the cyclotomic line (L0/selmer-specialization-control) and compare BF† with Kato's zeta elements of f and f ⊗ χ_K (as in FW §4.6.2–4.6.3), separating the two factors.

Remove the power of p as in FW §4.6.3: Kato's divisibility (KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction) and an integral local subspace along a line in Spec Λ_K reduce the integral statement to a cardinality at one generic arithmetic point.
acceptance: Export to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/fw-ordinary-theorem, which combines it with Kato's bound into the equality; RS-11 requires the KatoEulerSystems:L4 input inside this proof, not only in the consumer.
RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/22: this target lives in L2 (its inputs are L2's), not in L1; the canonical/Gross period comparison is a recorded gap, not a lemma.

nodes.title: Wan's ordinary GU(3,1) Rankin–Selberg divisibility
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with p = v_0v̄_0 split, f_0 a weight-two form of trivial character and square-free tame level N in an ordinary Hida family 𝐟, and ξ a Hecke character of infinity type (κ/2, −κ/2), κ ≥ 6 even, with ord_{v_0}, ord_{v̄_0} of its conductor ≤ 1. (Thm 1.1) If p ≥ 5, ξ|_{𝔸^×_ℚ} = ω∘Nm with κ ≡ 0 mod 2(p − 1), ρ̄_𝐟|_{G_K} irreducible, some q | N nonsplit in K with ρ̄_𝐟 ramified at q, the CM form g_ξ satisfies (dist) and (irred), every local root number ε(π_{f,v}, ξ_v, 1/2) = 1 at nonsplit v, and the conductor of ξ is divisible only by split primes, then L^{Hida}_{𝐟,ξ,K} ∈ Î^{ur}[[Γ_K]] and (L^{Hida}_{𝐟,ξ,K}) ⊇ char(X_{𝐟,K,ξ}). (Thm 1.2) For the single form f_0, if p ≥ 5, the p-adic avatar of ξ|·|^{κ/2}(ω^{-1}∘Nm) factors through Γ_K with κ ≡ 0 mod 2(p − 1), ρ̄_{f}|_{G_K} is irreducible and some q ∥ N is nonsplit in K, then (L_{f,ξ,K}) ⊇ char(X_{f,K,ξ}) as fractional ideals of Ô^{ur}_L[[Γ_K]] ⊗ L, allowing both global root numbers; this p-inverted, imprimitive two-variable bound (with the exceptional-prime and normality arguments of Wan20 §9) is the input exported to RankOneConverse.
hypotheses: As stated in Wan20 Thms 1.1–1.2; the published ordinary theorem (arXiv:1408.4044, Algebra Number Theory 2020), not the withdrawn arXiv:1412.1767 nor the nonordinary replacement (L2s).
proofSteps: Construct the Klingen Eisenstein family on U(3,1) whose constant terms are L^Σ_{𝐟,K,ξ} (Wan20 step (1)), with the Siegel section at p of Wan20 §4.3.

Fourier–Jacobi coprimality through the functional l_{θ⋆}, the doubling formula for U(2) × U(2) and Ichino's formula (Wan20 steps (2)–(5); L2s/fourier-jacobi-primitivity is the weight-two semi-ordinary analogue).

nodes.title: The residual hypotheses of the Fouquet–Wan and Nakamura theorems
nodes.statement: For an odd prime p, a finite field 𝔽 of characteristic p and an odd absolutely irreducible continuous ρ̄: G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) unramified outside a finite set Σ ∋ p, define the predicates: (A2.1) ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} is absolutely irreducible (p* = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p), and if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is an extension of χ_2 by χ_1 then χ_1^{-1}χ_2 ∉ {1, χ̄_cyc} (FW Assumption 2.1); (A3.5) if (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} = χ̄_1 ⊕ χ̄_2 then χ̄_1^{-1}χ̄_2 ≠ χ̄_cyc (FW Assumption 3.5); (A3.7) there is ℓ ∥ N, ℓ ≠ p, with dim_𝔽 ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1 (FW Assumption 3.7); (T1.7) (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc for every character χ̄, and there is ℓ ∤ p with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} a ramified extension 0 → µχ^{1−k/2}_cyc → ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} → µχ^{−k/2}_cyc → 0, µ unramified quadratic (nontrivial if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible) (FW Thm 1.7/5.1); and Nakamura's (N1) p ≥ 5, (N2) ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible, (N3) End_{𝔽[G_{ℚ_p}]}(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽, (N4) ρ̄_p not of the form (1 ∗; 0 ε^{±1}) ⊗ χ, (N5) ρ̄_p not of the form (1 ∗; 0 1) ⊗ χ (Nakamura Thm 1.1).
hypotheses: The predicates are on the residual representation only; the scalar exclusion (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄ is part of A2.1 through its second clause and the endomorphism remark after it (FW p. 17).
proofSteps: Record each predicate as a Prop on ρ̄ with its source.
Under A2.1 the endomorphisms of ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} are scalars unless (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄ (FW remark after Assumption 2.1), which is where Nakamura's N3 enters.
Nakamura's remark on N2/N5 (they can be dropped for the promodular ring) and FW's remark on p ≥ 5 (removed by Paškūnas–Tung's generalization) are recorded as API facts.
acceptance: Answers the consumer question of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures (source issue E1): whether FW Assumption 2.1(2)'s scalar exclusion is needed is decided by recording it as a separate predicate used by L3/universal-deformation-ring-structure and L3/nakamura-universal-zeta-morphism.

nodes.title: The universal deformation ring is a reduced complete intersection, finite free over Λ, and equal to the Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Under FW Assumption 2.1 (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses), the universal deformation ring R_Σ(ρ̄) of ρ̄ unramified outside Σ is a flat O-algebra which is a complete intersection of Krull dimension 4 (FW Prop. 2.4); there is a Zariski-dense open X^sm ⊂ Spec R_Σ(ρ̄) containing every point that is ordinary up to twist (if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is reducible) or crystalline and short up to twist (if irreducible), at which Spec R^χ_Σ(ρ̄) → Spec O is formally smooth, and R_Σ(ρ̄) is reduced (Cor. 2.5); the classical points (up to twist) are Zariski dense, so the surjection R_Σ(ρ̄) → 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} is an isomorphism (Prop. 2.6); and there is a regular sequence (x_1, x_2, x_3) in 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} making it a finite free module over Λ = O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]], such that classical points with the same image in Spec Λ are all crystalline-short (resp. ordinary) up to twist or none are (Cor. 2.7). Finite flatness over the regular ring Λ does not make R_Σ(ρ̄) regular; the main conjecture over R_Σ(ρ̄) is formulated through perfect complexes and the regular subring Λ.
hypotheses: FW Assumption 2.1; p odd; Σ finite containing p and the ramification of ρ̄.
The existence of a classical point of the Serre weight (FW cites Edixhoven/Gross–Coleman–Voloch-type results [31]) and the local deformation rings at p (ordinary or crystalline-short) are inputs.
proofSteps: Twisting by canonical square roots of characters in 1 + ϖO identifies R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ R^χ_Σ(ρ̄) ⊗̂ R_Σ(𝟙), reducing to fixed determinant (proof of FW Prop. 2.4).

Fixed determinant: the ordinary (resp. crystalline-short) quotient is cut out by a regular sequence (x_2, x_3) and is a finite Hecke algebra at a classical point; a presentation over the local rings gives the complete-intersection property (GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-presentation, global-dimension-lower-bound).

Étaleness over O[[X_2, X_3]] at the classical point gives X^sm (Cor. 2.5); density of classical points as in Böckle's argument gives R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ 𝕋 (Prop. 2.6; CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility:R31.6/boeckle-r-equals-t).
Choose x_1 from R_Σ(𝟙) to get the Λ-structure of Cor. 2.7.
acceptance: The Λ-structure depends on the initial classical point; the map Spec 𝕋 → Spec Λ may be ramified, even at classical points, but not at points of X^sm.
No axiom 'R = T' is imported: the isomorphism is proved from density of classical points and reducedness.
