nodes.title: Classical points of good reduction type exist and are dense
nodes.statement: Under FW Assumption 2.1: (i) if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible there is a crystalline and short classical point λ_f with R_Σ(ρ̄) ≅ R_Σ(ρ̄_f) (FW Lemma 2.2), and in general a point of Spec 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} that is crystalline-short, crystalline-short up to the quadratic twist ω^{(p−1)/2}, good ordinary, or good ordinary up to a quadratic twist (FW Lemma 2.8, used in the proof of Thm 5.1); (ii) X^sm is Zariski dense and the set of specializations that are not Iwasawa-suitable, or at which Spec 𝕋 is not étale over Spec Λ, has large codimension (FW Props 2.6, 3.16).
hypotheses: As stated; Iwasawa-suitable in the sense of FW Def. 3.19.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.2: twist so that the inertial weights are fundamental characters of level 2 and use the Serre weight conjecture (now a theorem) to produce a crystalline short form.
Lemma 2.8: the analogous statement covering the reducible-at-p case with ordinary points.
Density and codimension from Cor. 2.5 and Prop. 3.16.
acceptance: These are the seed points at which L4/etale-point-descent applies L2's crystalline theorem or the ordinary theorem.

nodes.title: Fundamental lines over the deformation ring and its quotients
nodes.statement: Let A be a quotient of 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} or of Λ (for example 𝕋, R(𝔞) = 𝕋/𝔞 for a minimal prime 𝔞, Λ, O_Iw or O) and T := T_Σ ⊗ A. The complexes RΓ_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T) and RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}, T) are perfect and commute with derived base change (FW Lemma 3.17). The Σ-partial fundamental line is the graded invertible A-module Δ_Σ(T) := Det^{-1}_A RΓ_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T) ⊗_A Det^{-1}_A T(−1)^+ (FW Def. 3.18); for A a domain and ℓ ∈ Σ prime to p put X_ℓ(T) := Det_A RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}/I_ℓ, T^{I_ℓ}) if rank T^{I_ℓ} ≠ 1 and Det_A[A —(1−α_ℓ)→ A] if rank T^{I_ℓ} = 1, and the fundamental line Δ(T) := Δ_Σ(T) ⊗ ⊗_{ℓ∈Σ}(X_ℓ(T) ⊗ Det^{-1}_A RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}, T)). Any ψ: A → A′ induces Δ_A(T) ⊗_A A′ ≅ Δ_{A′}(T′) for the Σ-partial line, and for the full line when ψ is Iwasawa-suitable; when both are defined, Δ_A(T) ≅ Det^{-1}RΓ_et(ℤ[1/p], T) ⊗ Det^{-1}T(−1)^+ (FW Prop. 3.20).
hypotheses: The determinant functor on perfect complexes is the Knudsen–Mumford functor (upstream PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras layer 5.1); T(−1)^+ is the +-part for complex conjugation.
proofSteps: Perfectness and base change of étale cohomology complexes (Nekovář's Selmer complexes, FW Lemma 3.17).
Define Δ_Σ and Δ by the determinant functor; the local factors X_ℓ use the explicit two-term complex when the inertia invariants have rank one.

Prop. 3.20: identify Δ with the {p}-partial line through the cone of RΓ(ℤ[1/Σ]) ⊕ ⊕RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}) → ⊕RΓ(G_{ℚ_ℓ}/I_ℓ, T^{I_ℓ}), and check base change of X_ℓ when ranks of inertia invariants agree and ψ(α_ℓ) = α′_ℓ.
acceptance: Fitting ideals commute with base change but are not principal; characteristic ideals are principal but not defined over the non-normal 𝕋. Fundamental lines are invertible and commute with arbitrary base change, which is why FW use them (FW §1.2.2, pp. 13–14).

nodes.title: Completed (co)homology localized at ρ̄ and its local–global factorization
nodes.statement: Under Nakamura's hypotheses (N1), (N3), (N4) (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses) and FW Assumption 2.1, there are G_ℚ × G_Σ-equivariant, 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear topological isomorphisms ρ^m ⊗_{𝕋} π^m_p ⊗̂_𝕋 π̃^m_{Σ_0} ≅ Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ} for Emerton's completed cohomology (Nakamura Thm 2.2; FW Thm 6.10, with π_p(ρ_Σ|_{G_{ℚ_p}}) from the p-adic local Langlands correspondence of Colmez, Emerton and Paškūnas, and π_ℓ the co-Whittaker modules attached to ρ_Σ|_{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} by the local Langlands correspondence in families), and its dual for the Borel–Moore completed homology H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗ (ρ^m)^* ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0} (Nakamura Cor. 2.5, the isomorphism φ_1 of §4.1). For ℓ ∈ Σ_0, the invariants π_ℓ(ρ)^U under U = K_1(ϖ^m) (m the conductor exponent) are free of rank one and commute with base change to classical points (FW Prop. 6.9, essential vectors).
hypotheses: (N1), (N3), (N4); in particular p ≥ 5, which is the range of PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp:R30.5's nodes. FW's extension to p = 3 rests on Paškūnas–Tung's generalization (FW remark after Thm 3.6), which the imported nodes do not cover; the request to R30.5 asks for it. The co-Whittaker families exist (Helm's local Langlands in families, conditional in general in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.5, proved in the GL_2 cases needed by FW Prop. 6.8).

nodes.title: The G_Σ-equivariant zeta morphism on completed homology
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 3, n ≥ 1 with prime(Np) = Σ and (n, Σ) = 1, Nakamura constructs from Kato's full-level Hecke-linear zeta classes a ℤ_p[GL_2(ℤ/N)]-linear map z^{Iw}_{N,n}(k, −): H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_k)(1) → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱^*_k(2)))_{Q_{k,n}} (Prop. 3.8, Q_{k,n} the multiplicative set of the smoothing factors); after localizing at the non-Eisenstein ideal of ρ̄ it lands in the unlocalized Iwasawa cohomology of H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_k)_ρ̄(2) (Cor. 3.14, Prop. 3.15); the limits over p-power level define a continuous 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Σ]-linear map z^{Iw}_{Σ,n,ρ̄}: H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) with z(τv) = σ_{−1}z(v) and the Euler-system norm relations (Thm 3.16); and the weight-k maps are recovered from weight two by tensoring with W = Sym^{k−2}(O²)^* (Prop. 3.17).
hypotheses: Localization at the non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of ρ̄ (absolutely irreducible) is what makes H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱) and H¹(Y(N), 𝒱) agree and the map integral.
proofSteps: Prop. 3.8: assemble Kato's classes c,d-z_{N,n}(k, r, r′) into a Hecke- and GL_2(ℤ/N)-equivariant map, removing the c,d smoothing in the localization Q_{k,n} (following Fukaya–Kato).

Prop. 3.15: integrality after localization at ρ̄, using freeness of Iwasawa cohomology over Λ^0 and the comparison of Kato's zeta values (the source's smoothing element d is corrected in PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E5).
Thm 3.16: pass to the limit over N_0p^∞ and over levels in Σ_0; Prop. 3.17 compares weights.
acceptance: The modular input is imported from KatoEulerSystems:L2 (full-level Hecke-linear zeta classes), which says the universal-deformation map is owned here.

nodes.title: Nakamura's universal zeta morphism
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄: G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) satisfy (N1)–(N5) of L3/fw-residual-hypotheses (or (N1), (N3), (N4) with R_{ρ̄,Σ} replaced by the promodular ring 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ}), with universal deformation ρ^u over R_{ρ̄,Σ}. There is a family of R_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear maps z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u): (ρ^u)^* → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], (ρ^u)^*(1)), n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, such that (i) z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(τv) = σ_{−1}z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(v) for complex conjugation τ; (ii) Cor ∘ z_{Σ,nl}(ρ^u) = z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if l | n and P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if (l, n) = 1; (iii) at every point x_f of Spec R_{ρ̄,Σ}(ℚ̄_p) attached to a newform f, z_{Σ,1}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ∖{p}} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z(f) with P_{f,l}(u) = det(1 − Frob_l u | ρ_f^{I_l}) (Nakamura Thm 1.1, Cor. 4.2, Thm 4.3). Condition (i) makes z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) an R ⊗̂ Λ_n-linear map on (ρ^u)^* ⊗̂_{ℤ_p[±1]} Λ_n (Remark 1.2). It is defined by transporting z^{Iw}_{Σ,n,ρ̄} along φ_1 (L3/completed-homology-factorization), factoring out the projective envelope P̃ and applying the Whittaker functor Ψ_{Σ_0} at the primes of Σ_0 (§4.1, Lemma 4.1).
hypotheses: (N1)–(N5); FW's version (FW Thm 3.6) works under Assumptions 2.1 and 3.5 and removes p ≥ 5 via Paškūnas–Tung's generalization of the relevant local results (FW remark after Thm 3.6).
proofSteps: Lemma 4.1: φ_1 induces an isomorphism H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗̂ H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^m)^*(1) ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0}), via a perfect complex computing Iwasawa cohomology.

Remove the factor (π^m_p)^* using Paškūnas's identification of P̃ with the dual of the universal deformation of π̄ (removing-projective-envelope), and apply the Whittaker functor to π̃^m_{Σ_0}, which is co-Whittaker so that Ψ_{Σ_0}(π̃) ≅ 𝕋 (§4.1).
Properties (i)–(ii) follow from Thm 3.16 (Cor. 4.2); (iii) is L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem.
acceptance: It is the morphism FW call z_Σ: T_Σ(−1)^+ → H¹(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) (FW Thm 3.6) after the identifications of FW §3.2.1.

nodes.title: The universal zeta morphism specializes to Kato's
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Nakamura §4 ((N1), (N3), (N4)), for every modular point x_f ∈ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(E) attached to a newform f ∈ S_k(Γ_1(N_f))^{new} of weight k ≥ 2 and every n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, z_{Σ,n}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(f) as maps V′_1(f)_E → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], V′_1(f)_E(1)) under V′_1(f)_E ≅ ρ_f^* (55), where z_n(f) is Kato's (Nakamura-twisted) zeta morphism and Σ_0 = Σ ∖ {p}; the equality does not depend on the choice of (55) since End_{E[G_ℚ]}(ρ_f) = E (Nakamura Thm 4.3, Remark 4.4). In particular the morphism specializes to the Kato class used in KatoEulerSystems:L3–L4.
hypotheses: (N1), (N3), (N4); x_f modular.
proofSteps: Let τ be the Galois type of ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} and ⋄ = cr or st; x_f factors through Kisin's potentially semistable (crystalline) quotient R^⋄_p(k, τ) (Nakamura Thm 4.5).

Paškūnas's result (Thm 4.7) makes M^⋄(k, τ) ⊗ 𝕋^⋄ free of rank one at x_f; Cor. 4.8 and Prop. 4.9 identify σ^⋄(k, τ) ⊗ H̃^{BM}_{1,ρ̄,Σ} with the classical cohomology H¹_{Σ_0}(𝒱^*_{k/E}(σ^⋄(τ)))_ρ̄(1).

Under these identifications z_{Σ,n}(f) is the base change of Ψ_{Σ_0}(z^{Iw}_{Σ_0,n,ρ̄}(k, σ^⋄(τ), −)); comparing motivic structures with Kato's construction (Nakamura §4.4, (68)–(78)) gives the equality with the Euler factors at Σ_0.
acceptance: The Euler factors at Σ_0 are exactly those of NakamuraZeta.classical; dropping them would contradict the change-of-Σ formula (79).

nodes.title: The zeta trivialization of the fundamental line
nodes.statement: Let z_Σ: T_Σ(−1)^+ → H¹_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) be Nakamura's zeta morphism (FW Thm 3.6). Since H²_et(ℤ[1/Σ], T_Σ) is torsion and H¹ has generic rank equal to that of T_Σ(−1)^+ over 𝕋 (or over Λ), z_Σ determines an injective trivialization triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Q(𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄}), equivalently an isomorphism Δ_Σ ≅ (x/y)𝕋 for an invertible fractional ideal (FW (1.2.1)); over Λ it gives triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac Λ (Conj. 3.30's map). For every specialization λ: 𝕋 → R(𝔞) to a minimal prime and every classical point λ_f: R(𝔞) → O_Iw there are commutative diagrams relating triv_{z_Σ}, triv_{z(𝔞)} and triv_{z(f)_Iw} (FW (1.2.2), (1.2.3), Props 3.22–3.23), and for Iwasawa-suitable λ the same holds for the full fundamental lines with Euler factors.
hypotheses: FW Assumptions 2.1, 3.5; the specializations in the diagrams with full lines are Iwasawa-suitable (Def. 3.19).
proofSteps: Torsion of H² and the rank of H¹ over the total fraction ring (Kato's results at classical points, density) make Det^{-1}RΓ ⊗ Det^{-1}T(−1)^+ ⊗ Q(𝕋) canonically trivial once a generator of the image of z_Σ is chosen.
Compatibility with base change (L3/fundamental-line) and with specialization of z_Σ (L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem) gives the diagrams (FW Props 3.22–3.23).
Over Λ, view T_Σ as a free Λ-module of rank 2d and repeat (FW proof of Prop. 5.5).
acceptance: The universal main conjecture is the statement that the image of triv_{z_Σ} is 𝕋 (resp. Λ); over the non-factorial 𝕋 this cannot be deduced from pointwise statements, which is why the family statement is made over Λ.

nodes.title: Kato's generalized main conjecture for the universal family and its specializations
nodes.statement: For an Iwasawa-suitable specialization λ: 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} → S (S a regular domain), the generalized main conjecture for λ is the proposition that the trivialization triv_{z(λ)} of L3/zeta-trivialization is an isomorphism Δ(T_λ) ≅ S (FW Conjs 3.24–3.25; at a classical point λ(f)_Iw: 𝕋 → O_Iw this is Kato's main conjecture, FW Conj. 1.5 / Conj. 3.24); for a minimal prime 𝔞 it is Δ(T(𝔞)) ≅ R(𝔞) (Conj. 3.27); and the universal-family conjecture is the proposition that triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac Λ induces Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ over the regular subring Λ = O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]] (Conj. 3.30, Kato's Conjecture 3.2.2 for (Spec ℤ[1/Σ], Λ, T_Σ)). The stronger statement over 𝕋 itself (Conj. 3.26) is a separate proposition.
hypotheses: The propositions are stated, not assumed; Λ-structure as in L3/universal-deformation-ring-structure.
proofSteps: Define each conjecture as the proposition that the image of the corresponding trivialization is the unit fractional ideal.
Record the implications: Conj. 3.26 (over 𝕋) ⇒ Conj. 3.30 (over Λ) by restriction of scalars; Conj. 3.30 ⇒ Conj. 3.24 at classical points is FW Prop. 5.8 (L4/family-to-point-limit).

nodes.title: The zeta trivialization over Λ is integral
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1, the trivialization triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac(Λ) of L3/zeta-trivialization sends Δ_Σ(T_Σ)^{-1} into Λ; equivalently its image is αΛ for some α ∈ Λ (FW Prop. 5.5).
hypotheses: FW Thm 5.1's residual hypotheses; Λ = O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]] factorial and regular.
proofSteps: Suppose the image of Δ^{-1} is (x/y)Λ with x/y ∉ Λ; since Λ is factorial there is a height-one prime 𝔭 = (y_0) containing y but not x.

By density (L3/smooth-classical-points) choose an Iwasawa-suitable λ_Iw, étale over Λ, with λ(y_0) ∈ m^n_{O_Iw} and λ(x) ∉ m^n for large n; at such a point T_{λ,Iw} is a lattice in a direct sum of classical representations V_{λ,r,Iw}.

Kato's one-sided divisibility at each classical point (KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction, integral where T_{λ,Iw} has the needed image) gives triv(Δ^{-1}) ⊆ O_Iw at λ, contradicting λ(x/y) ∉ O_Iw.
acceptance: This uses only Kato's divisibility and density; Zariski density alone is not used to conclude that a rational section is an integral generator — the height-one prime argument over the factorial Λ is.

sources.match: The image of Δ_Σ(T_Σ)^{-1} lies in Λ, by a height-one prime of the factorial ring Λ and Kato's bound at well-chosen classical points.

nodes.title: From pointwise main conjectures at an étale point to the family over Λ
nodes.statement: Suppose there is a point x: Λ → O at which Spec 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} → Spec Λ is étale and every point ψ: 𝕋 → O above x satisfies Kato's main conjecture (FW Conj. 3.24). Then triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ↪ Frac(Λ) is an isomorphism onto Λ (FW Prop. 5.7).
hypotheses: As stated; all λ_Iw above x are Iwasawa-suitable because of étaleness.
proofSteps: By L4/integrality-of-universal-trivialization the image of Δ^{-1} is αΛ with α ∈ Λ.

Specialize along x_Iw: by the base-change diagram (FW Prop. 3.23; L3/zeta-trivialization), x_Iw(α)O_Iw is the product over ψ ∈ S_x of the pointwise images, each O_Iw by hypothesis, so x_Iw(α) is a unit.
An element of the local ring Λ whose specialization is a unit is a unit; hence αΛ = Λ.
acceptance: The descent is over the regular ring Λ, not over 𝕋: over the non-factorial 𝕋 an invertible module trivial at a point need not be trivial.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's universal-family main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄: G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) satisfy the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1 (absolutely irreducible; (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc; a prime ℓ ∤ p with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} a ramified extension of µχ^{−k/2}_cyc by µχ^{1−k/2}_cyc, µ unramified and nontrivial if ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible). For Σ finite, viewing the universal deformation T_Σ as a free module over Λ ≅ O[[X_1, X_2, X_3]], the zeta morphism z_Σ induces an isomorphism triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ (FW Thm 5.2 = Thm 1.8; Kato's Conjecture 3.2.2 for (Spec ℤ[1/Σ], Λ, T_Σ)). The statement is over the regular subring Λ; the stronger statement over 𝕋 ≅ R_Σ(ρ̄) itself is not asserted.
hypotheses: FW Thm 5.1's residual hypotheses (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses, T1.7) together with Assumptions 2.1 and 3.5 where the construction of z_Σ needs them.
proofSteps: Find a seed point: by FW Lemma 2.8 (L3/smooth-classical-points) there is a classical point that is crystalline-short, crystalline-short up to the quadratic twist ω^{(p−1)/2}, good ordinary, or good ordinary up to quadratic twist.

At such a point Kato's main conjecture holds (FW Prop. 5.6): crystalline-short points by L2/fw-crystalline-main-conjecture (Thm 4.51), ordinary points by the ordinary theorem — the ordinary seed is the equality of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/fw-ordinary-theorem, which combines L2/fw-ordinary-reverse-bound with Kato's bound; twists are handled in the same way.
Points near the seed that are étale over Λ and of the same type satisfy the pointwise conjecture; apply L4/etale-point-descent.
acceptance: Exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/fw-universal-family-theorem; the determinant over Λ must not be read as a statement over the deformation ring.

nodes.title: From the family over Λ to every classical point
nodes.statement: Suppose triv_{z_Σ}: Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ (L4/fw-universal-family-theorem). Then for every classical point λ(f): 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} → O, including points ramified over Λ, triv_{z(f)_Iw}: Δ_Σ(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw, i.e. Kato's main conjecture holds for λ(f) (FW Prop. 5.8).
hypotheses: As stated; the Σ-partial lines and the Euler-factor-corrected morphisms are used, which both commute with specialization at a classical point even if it is ramified over Λ.
proofSteps: Kato's divisibility gives triv_{z(f)_Iw}(Δ_Σ(T(f)_Iw)^{-1}) ⊆ O_Iw, so its image is (1/γ)O_Iw.
Over 𝕋 write the image of Δ_Σ as (α/β)𝕋 with λ(f)_Iw(β) ≠ 0 (FW Prop. 3.23).
Choose λ close to λ(f), outside the zero set of β, étale over Λ with all points above Iwasawa-suitable; the family isomorphism forces each pointwise γ_ψ to be a unit there, so λ_Iw(α/β) is a unit.
By continuity, taking λ close to λ(f), 1/γ = λ(f)_Iw(α/β) is a unit.
acceptance: A specialization at which a value vanishes is never cancelled: the argument avoids the zero set of β and works with the Euler-factor-corrected lines.

nodes.title: Fouquet–Wan's main conjecture at every point of the family
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(Np^r)) a normalized eigencuspform of weight k ≥ 2 whose residual representation satisfies the hypotheses of FW Thm 5.1 (L3/fw-residual-hypotheses, T1.7), with the auxiliary prime ℓ satisfying ℓ ∥ N. Then the zeta morphism gives an isomorphism triv_{z(f)_Iw}: Δ_{O_Iw}(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw (FW Thm 5.1 = Thm 1.7); equivalently char_{Λ_Iw}H²(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw) = char_{Λ_Iw}H¹(ℤ[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw. This covers non-ordinary and bad-reduction points at p (π(f)_p principal series, Steinberg or supercuspidal) and needs no µ-invariant hypothesis. Consequences: Sel_ℚ(f) is finite iff L(f, k/2) ≠ 0 (Cor. 5.3), and for an abelian variety of GL_2-type with L(A,1) ≠ 0 satisfying the hypotheses, the p-part of the BSD formula holds (Cor. 5.4).
hypotheses: As stated; the scalar case (ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}})^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄ is not excluded by Thm 5.1's displayed hypotheses but enters through Assumptions 2.1/3.5 used for the deformation ring and z_Σ (source issue ModularIwasawaMainConjectures/E1, which this packet adopts).
proofSteps: Apply L4/fw-universal-family-theorem to ρ̄_f.
Apply L4/family-to-point-limit at λ(f) (FW proof of Thm 5.1, p. 73).
Translate the fundamental-line statement into characteristic ideals over the regular O_Iw (L3/kato-generalized-main-conjecture, GenMC.point_iff_kato).
acceptance: Exported to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-pointwise-theorem in the cohomological (Kato) form; the signed or ordinary scalar versions are the consumer's, after its separate local comparison.

nodes.title: Euler factors, Tor terms and the regular subring in specialization
nodes.statement: For a specialization λ: A → A′ between quotients of 𝕋^Σ_{m_ρ̄} or Λ: (i) the Σ-partial fundamental line commutes with every base change, Δ_Σ(T) ⊗ A′ ≅ Δ_Σ(T′); (ii) the full fundamental line commutes with λ when λ is Iwasawa-suitable, the Euler-factor lines X_ℓ(T) specializing to X_ℓ(T′) because the ranks of inertia invariants and the eigenvalues α_ℓ are preserved (FW Prop. 3.20); otherwise the rank of T^{I_ℓ} can jump and the comparison acquires the factor relating X_ℓ(T) ⊗ A′ and X_ℓ(T′); (iii) Nakamura's change-of-Σ formula z_{Σ′,n} ⊗ id = ∏_{l∈Σ′∖Σ} P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n} matches the passage from Δ_{Σ′} to Δ_Σ with the Euler factors P_l; (iv) a statement over the regular subring Λ (FW Thm 1.8) is a statement about T_Σ as a Λ-module of rank 2d, and at a point x of Λ it is a statement about the product over all points of 𝕋 above x — it implies the statement over 𝕋 only at points étale over Λ, and at ramified points only through L4/family-to-point-limit.
hypotheses: As stated; Iwasawa-suitable as in FW Def. 3.19.
proofSteps: (i)–(ii): perfectness and derived base change of RΓ (FW Lemma 3.17), and the explicit two-term complexes defining X_ℓ (FW Prop. 3.20's proof).
(iii): Nakamura (79) and the exact sequence relating H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ]) and H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ′]) through ⊕_{l∈Σ′∖Σ}H²_Iw(ℚ_l) (Nakamura proof of Thm 5.7, (78)–(79)).
(iv): restriction of scalars along the finite free Λ → 𝕋 and the étale-point analysis of FW Props 5.7–5.8.
acceptance: Lattice corrections: when T(f)_Iw is replaced by a different G_ℚ-stable lattice the fundamental line changes by the index, so the lattice is the one coming from T_Σ (FW notation T(f)_Iw = T(𝔞) ⊗ O_Iw).

nodes.title: Congruences between Kato's zeta morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f, g be normalized newforms with coefficients in E, ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible, and the assumptions of Nakamura §4 holding for ρ̄ = ρ̄_f. If f ≡ g modulo ϖ^m (Hecke eigenvalues congruent at all but finitely many primes), then ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(f) ≡ ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{g,l}(σ_l^{-1})·z_n(g) modulo ϖ^m as maps ρ^*_{f,m} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], ρ^*_{f,m}(1)) (Nakamura Cor. 5.6).
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions ((N1), (N3), (N4)); Σ containing the levels of f and g and p.
proofSteps: x_f and x_g are points of the same Spec 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} that agree modulo ϖ^m (the printed ϖ^n in the proof is ϖ^m, PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E11).
Both Euler-corrected zeta morphisms are specializations of the one universal z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) (L3/nakamura-specialization-theorem), so they agree modulo ϖ^m.
acceptance: This is the congruence of zeta morphisms that propagates Kato's main conjecture along congruences (L4/nakamura-lambda-defect).

nodes.title: The residual zeta morphism and the space of points X(ρ̄)
nodes.statement: Let Σ_ρ̄ = {p} ∪ ram(ρ̄). For Σ_ρ̄ ⊆ Σ ⊆ Σ′, ρ^m_{Σ′} ⊗ 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} ≅ ρ^m_Σ and z_{Σ′,n}(ρ^m_{Σ′}) ⊗ id = ∏_{l∈Σ′∖Σ} P_l(σ_l^{-1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m_Σ) (Nakamura (79)). The residual zeta morphism z_{Σ,n}(ρ̄) is the base change of z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) to 𝔽, a Λ_{n,𝔽}-linear map ρ̄^* ⊗_{𝔽[±1]} Λ_{n,𝔽} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σn, ζ_n], ρ̄^*(1)). Put X(ρ̄) = ∪_Σ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(ℤ̄_p) with its modular points X(ρ̄)^{mod}, and for a character η of Δ = Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ) consider η-components over Λ^η.
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions; absolute irreducibility of ρ̄.
proofSteps: Base change of z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) along 𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ} → 𝔽, using that H¹_Iw is computed by a perfect complex.
Compatibility with change of Σ from (79).
acceptance: The residual morphism carries the information of the whole family: its nonvanishing is equivalent to µ = 0 at one, hence every, modular point (L4/nakamura-residual-structure).

nodes.title: Residual nonvanishing, µ = 0 and the structure of residual Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a character η of Δ. (i) The following are equivalent: z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η ≠ 0; µ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1))^η/Im(z_1(f)^η)) = 0 for some x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^{mod}; the same for all x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^{mod} (Nakamura Thm 5.7; the published version adds Conj. 5.8 that these always hold). (ii) Assume X(ρ̄)^{mod}_a ≠ ∅ (modular points with Nakamura's condition (a)) and (i) holds for η. Then H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_𝔽, and H¹_Iw/Im(z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η) and H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η are finite-dimensional (arXiv Thm 5.8 = published Thm 5.9); the η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄ is the equality of their dimensions (arXiv Conj. 5.9 = published 5.10). (iii) For every x ∈ Spec(𝕋_{ρ̄,Σ})(O) ⊂ X(ρ̄): H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_O; the quotient by Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η and H²_Iw are torsion with µ = 0; and if x is modular, or there is τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) with (ρ_x/(τ−1)ρ_x)[1/p] one-dimensional, then Char(H¹_Iw/Im z^η) ⊆ Char(H²_Iw^η) (arXiv Thm 5.10 = published Thm 5.11).
hypotheses: Nakamura §4 assumptions; (ii)–(iii) assume X(ρ̄)^{mod}_a ≠ ∅ and (i) for η.
proofSteps: (i): the mod-ϖ exact sequences relating H¹_Iw(ρ_f^*(1))/ϖ and H¹_Iw(ρ̄^*(1)), freeness of H¹_Iw (Kato Thm 12.4(3)) and L4/zeta-morphism-congruences.
(ii): Kato's theorem 5.2 at a point of X^{mod}_a gives the rank and finiteness; descend modulo ϖ.

(iii): lift freeness and torsion from the residual statement; µ = 0 from (i); the divisibility from the Euler system bound (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8 / KatoEulerSystems:L4) under the image condition.
acceptance: µ = 0 is a hypothesis-free consequence only of residual nonvanishing; it is not assumed.

nodes.title: The λ-defect is constant on the family and Kato's main conjecture propagates along congruences
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of L4/nakamura-residual-structure (ii), for every x ∈ X(ρ̄): λ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η) − λ(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η) equals dim_𝔽(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η) − dim_𝔽 H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η, hence is independent of x (arXiv Thm 5.13 = published Thm 5.14); consequently the η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄ holds iff the weak (λ-) version holds for some x iff it holds for all x (arXiv Cor. 5.14 = published Cor. 5.15). In particular (Nakamura Thm 1.4): if g_1, g_2, g_3 are congruent to f with (1) some τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) making ρ_{g_1}/(τ − 1)ρ_{g_1} free of rank one over O, (2) µ = 0 for g_2, and (3) Kato's main conjecture for g_3, then µ = 0 and Kato's main conjecture hold for f.
hypotheses: As in L4/nakamura-residual-structure; the proof's last display prints H¹ for H² (PAPER-NAKAMURA-23/E12, corrected).
proofSteps: For a module with µ = 0, λ(M) = λ_𝔽(M/ϖ) − λ_𝔽(M[ϖ]) (Nakamura (92)); apply it to H¹_Iw/Im z and to H²_Iw and use the residual comparison (91).
The residual side does not depend on x, giving constancy; the corollary follows since for µ = 0 and the inclusion of (iii), equality of λ-invariants is equality of characteristic ideals.
Thm 1.4 is the specialization of these statements to modular points, as in Kim–Lee–Ponsinet.
acceptance: Gives the pointwise consequences of the universal zeta element that stage L4 owns (Nakamura §5); the conjectures are recorded as propositions, not assumed.

nodes.title: The ordinary elliptic-curve refinement: aggregate of the endpoints
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ and a prime p of good ordinary reduction, stage L5 collects, without a second proof, the two reverse-divisibility endpoints planned in this roadmap: (a) Burungale–Castella–Skinner's cyclotomic theorem — for p > 3 with E[p] irreducible, X_ord(E/ℚ_∞) is Λ-torsion and char_Λ X_ord(E/ℚ_∞) = (L_p(E/ℚ)) in Λ ⊗ ℚ_p, with equality in Λ under the rank-one image condition (im) (BCS Thm 1.1.2), proved in L5b from L5a's early product input and four Kato bounds; and (b) Fouquet–Wan's cohomological theorem at good ordinary points (L4/fw-pointwise-theorem, through L2/fw-ordinary-reverse-bound). The scalar ordinary main conjecture with canonical periods, the curve-to-form lattice and Manin-constant transport and the final assembly are ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L1–L3's, which import the endpoints directly from L5b and L4.
hypotheses: Hypotheses are those of each endpoint; nothing is added or removed here.
RS-11: L5 is an aggregate only; it is not a prerequisite of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3 (the requested cut C.L5 → I.L3).
proofSteps: List the endpoints with their owners: AutomorphicCongruences:L5b/rational-cyclotomic-endpoint and L5b/integral-cyclotomic-endpoint for (a), L4/fw-pointwise-theorem for (b).
Record that the BCS rational/integral distinction survives: (a) is in Λ ⊗ ℚ_p without (im) and in Λ with (im).
acceptance: Acceptance of the roadmap: opposite divisibilities on the same integral objects as Kato's; no hidden 'assume the divisibility' field; the BCS rational/integral distinction kept.

nodes.title: Interface: the ordinary two-variable Perrin-Riou/Greenberg equivalence (BCS Theorem 4.1.3, Corollary 4.1.4)
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform, p ∤ 2N an ordinary prime for g, and K imaginary quadratic with p split (spl), (D_K, N) = 1 and ρ̄_g irreducible over G_K (irr_K). The following are equivalent: (i) X_ord(g/K_∞) is Λ_K-torsion and (L^{PR}_p(g/K)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g/K_∞)) in Λ_K ⊗ ℚ_p; (ii) X_Gr(g/K_∞) is Λ_K-torsion and (L^{Gr}_p(g/K)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_Gr(g/K_∞)) in Λ^{ur}_K ⊗ ℚ_p; the same holds for the opposite divisibilities and before inverting p (BCS Thm 4.1.3, from BSTW §9.3.2). For two newforms g, g′ with p ∤ 2NN′ ordinary for both and K satisfying (spl), (D_K, NN′) = 1 and (irr_K) for both, the product statements (L^{PR}_p(g/K)·L^{PR}_p(g′/K)) ⊇ ch(X_ord(g/K_∞))·ch(X_ord(g′/K_∞)) and (L^{Gr}_p(g/K)·L^{Gr}_p(g′/K)) ⊇ ch(X_Gr(g/K_∞))·ch(X_Gr(g′/K_∞)) are equivalent, in either direction (BCS Cor. 4.1.4). This node states the exact contract L5a consumes; its proof (the ordinary BSTW two-variable zeta element, both explicit reciprocity laws, and the two four-term Poitou–Tate sequences) belongs to the planned owner KatoEulerSystems L5 of RS-11, which does not yet exist.
hypotheses: The ordinary BSTW construction needs E[p](K) = 0-type vanishing (van_K) for the integral comparison and the stated split-field, discriminant and irreducibility hypotheses; without van_K only the p-inverted comparison is available (RS-11 ordinaryBSTW contract).
BCS cite the theorem as Proposition 4.1.3 in the proof of Prop. 5.2.1; it is Thm 4.1.3 in v2 (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/29).
proofSteps: Writing H for the rank-one global module, Z for the two-variable zeta class and X_st for the strict Selmer dual, the two Poitou–Tate sequences give ch(H/ΛZ)·ch(X_Gr) = (L_Gr)·ch(X_st) and ch(H/ΛZ)·ch(X_ord) = (L_PR)·ch(X_st) after the unramified coefficient extension, using both explicit reciprocity laws (RS-11 handoff).
Prove rank one, torsion and nonvanishing of the terms before cancelling; this gives ch(X_Gr)·(L_PR) = ch(X_ord)·(L_Gr), hence both directions of the equivalence.
Cor. 4.1.4: direct sums of the two pairs of sequences for g and g′.
acceptance: Does not use the anticyclotomic Theorem 4.2.1, which belongs to HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8/HE.8b.

nodes.title: Restricting the quartic-CM characteristic ideal to K
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform, p > 3 a good ordinary prime with ρ̄_g irreducible, F a real quadratic field, K imaginary quadratic, M = FK the quartic CM field, K̃_∞ = FK_∞, Λ̃_K = O[[Gal(K̃_∞/M)]] ≅ Λ_K and π_K: Λ_M → Λ̃_K ≅ Λ_K induced by Gal(M_∞/M) ↠ Gal(K̃_∞/M). Then π_K(ch_{Λ_M}(X_ord(g/M_∞))) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g/K_∞))·ch_{Λ_K}(X_ord(g^F/K_∞)) in Λ_K, where g^F is the twist of g by the quadratic character of F/ℚ (BCS Lemma 5.1.1).
hypotheses: As in BCS §5; the containment is integral and in the stated direction only.
proofSteps: Shapiro's lemma and the control results (L0/selmer-specialization-control; SU Props 3.6–3.7 in the journal numbering) identify H¹_{F_Λ}(M, M_g)[I_K] with H¹_{F_Λ}(M, T_g ⊗ Λ̃^∨_K) ≅ H¹_{F_Λ}(M, T_g ⊗ Λ^∨_K) ⊕ H¹_{F_Λ}(M, T_g ⊗ η_F ⊗ Λ^∨_K), with T_g ⊗ η_F ≅ T_{g^F}.
Restriction from M to K of a module induced along Gal(M/K) ≅ Gal(F/ℚ) splits by the characters of Gal(M/K) (Shapiro).
SU Cor. 3.8 (journal): π_K(ch_{Λ_M}(X)) ⊇ ch_{Λ_K}(X/I_K) (L0/selmer-specialization-control (ii)).
acceptance: Direction check: the image of the quartic characteristic ideal contains the product of the two K-characteristic ideals, so a divisibility for M gives one for the product over K.

nodes.title: Existence of the auxiliary fields K and F
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be an elliptic newform and p ≥ 5 a prime of good ordinary reduction with ρ̄_g irreducible over G_ℚ. There exist an imaginary quadratic K satisfying (disc) (D_K odd, D_K ≠ −3), (Heeg) (every ℓ | N splits in K), (spl) (p splits in K) and (irr_K), and a real quadratic F with (i) p inert in F, (ii) D_F odd with every prime dividing D_F split in K, (iii) every ℓ | N inert in F if ℓ ≡ −1 mod p and split otherwise, (iv) (irr_M) for M = FK, (v) ρ̄_g|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} irreducible, (vi) F ≠ ℚ(ζ_5)^+ if p = 5 (BCS Lemma 5.2.3). Moreover such M/F satisfies (pN, D_F) = 1, (N O_F, D_{M/F}) = 1, (spl_F) and (Δ), and n^- = O_F, so the hypotheses of Wan's theorem (L5w) other than Hypothesis 3.1.1 hold, and (H1)–(H3) follow from (v), (vi), the minimal-lift argument and (iii) (proof of BCS Prop. 5.2.1).
hypotheses: As stated; the conditions are independent splitting conditions satisfied by a positive proportion of quadratic fields.
proofSteps: Since p ∤ N, conditions (i) and (iii) on F are independent splitting conditions; fix F with odd D_F.
Similarly (spl), (Heeg) and (ii) hold for a positive proportion of K; choose one with (disc) and (irr_K).

(irr_M) holds if FK is not in the splitting field of ρ_g|_{G_K}; if ρ̄_g|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is reducible, ρ̄_g|_{G_F} is induced from an index-two subgroup containing G_{F(ζ_p)}, which forces p = 5 and F = ℚ(ζ_5)^+.
